has made me cling to my Lord, like the black-bee, that is caught in the woven lotus flower.

O Kabir! (Just as this ego comes to lead others astray,) it came to me too, in many forms.
Kabeer, she came to me in various forms and disguises.
Kabir, mammon came to me, assuming various garbs.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this deceiving Maya, taking countless guises, came to me to deceive me.
584S: Ham = me. Un = she (the ego). Aades = salutation. Un...aades = that ego bowed, that ego bent, that ego changed into humility. ||8||
But my beloved True Guru saved me (from it); that ego bowed down (that ego changed into humility). ||8||
My Guru saved me, and now she bows humbly to me. ||8||
My Guru saved me and she make me obeisance.
But from the deception of that Maya, the teaching of our own Guru has saved us; and that Maya, knowing me to be unshakeable, bowed to me. ||8||
DBAT: Soee = this ego alone. Jih mooai = by whose death, by the death of which ego.
O Kabir! This ego alone should be killed, by whose death there is peace.
Kabeer, kill only that, which, when killed, shall bring peace.
Kabir, destroy you only that, by whose death, you may be blessed with peace.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, kill that one alone — meaning, kill ego alone — by killing which this being has peace.
H6JM: Sabh ko = everyone. Bhalo bhalo kahai = (everyone) praises (giving up ego). Koe buro na maanai = no one calls (killing ego) a bad deed. ||9||
Everyone praises the giving up of ego; no one calls this deed bad. ||9||
Everyone shall call you good, very good, and no one shall think you are bad. ||9||
Then every one shall call you good and virtuous and no one shall deem you bad.
Everyone calls the one who is free of ego good; no one thinks them bad. ||9||
CP6C: Kaareea = black, dark. Oobhe = stand up, set out. Kaare jant = black beings, people with black hearts, thieves and other wicked people.
O Kabir! When the nights are dark, thieves and other black-hearted people rise up (from their homes),
Kabeer, the night is dark, and men go about doing their dark deeds.
When the nights are dark, the men with dark deeds arise, says Kabir.

Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, those in whose inner mind the (kaare) fear-giving beasts of lust and the rest (oobhe) stand — that is, are settled — their nights, which are the stages of life, have become black with sins. Or: Kabir ji says, on dark nights thieves stand ready with nooses.

NHKM: Lai = taking. Uth dhaavte = rise up and run. Si = such people. Jaan = know, understand, be sure. Maare bhagvant = struck down by God, far from God. ||10||
take nooses and set out (to rob others' homes), but know for sure that such people are struck down by God. ||10||
They take the noose and run around; but rest assured that God shall destroy them. ||10||
And taking nooses with them, they run about, however, know you that they are the accursed of the Lord.

They run with nooses and other weapons to kill beings. Knowing them to be sinners, Bhagvan Himself kills them through the fearsome Yama and the rest; so even if they are living, know them to be struck down by Bhagvant. ||10||
SHYE: Birva = small plant. Berrhio = surrounded, encircled. Palaas = palaah, chhichhra tree.
O Kabir! Know even a small sandalwood plant to be good, even if it is surrounded by trees like dhak and palaah.
Kabeer, the sandalwood tree is good, even though it is surrounded by weeds.
Kabir, good is the sandal tree, even when it may be surrounded by the buteafrondosa trees.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as the sandalwood (birva) tree, which is excellent, is (berrhio) surrounded by a (dhaak) crowd of palaas trees —
0GGX: Oe = those dhak and palaah trees. Ju = the trees that. Base = dwell, have grown. Paas = near. ||11||
those (worthless trees like dhak and palaah) that grow near the sandalwood also become sandalwood. ||11||
Those who dwell near the sandalwood tree, become just like the sandalwood tree. ||11||
Those, who live near the sandal trees; they too become like sandal.

the palaas that dwell near that sandalwood have also become the very form of sandalwood. Example: ☬ the sandalwood of the saints is surrounded by the palaas of seekers. The seekers who dwell near the saints also become spiritually wise and take on the very form of the saints. ||11||
13V3: Badaaee = in pride, in the pride of being tall. Boodia = know it drowned. Koe = any of you. Iu = like this. Mat doobahu = do not drown.
O Kabir! The bamboo plant is drowned in the pride (of being tall); let none of you drown (in ego) like the bamboo, because
Kabeer, the bamboo is drowned in its egotistical pride. No one should drown like this.
Kabir, the bamboo, is drowned in its ego. Let no one drown oneself like this.
Sri Kabir ji says: let no one drown in the way the bamboo has drowned in its own greatness.
JA89: even if bamboo grows near sandalwood, the fragrance of sandalwood does not come into it. ||12||
Bamboo also dwells near the sandalwood tree, but it does not take up its fragrance. ||12||
Bamboo abides near the sandal tree, however, it become not fragrant.
The bamboo lives right near the sandalwood, but the fragrance of sandalwood never enters it. ||12|| ☬ See the inner meaning of this salok in the salok of the Gatha.
8WST: Deen = religion, dharma. Siu = for the sake of.
O Kabir! The heedless person lost 'deen' (faith) for the sake of 'dunia' (worldly wealth), (and at the end this) world did not go along with them either.
Kabeer, the mortal loses his faith, for the sake of the world, but the world shall not go along with him in the end.
Kabir, for the sake of the world, man loses his faith, however, the world goes not with him.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, the (dunee) Maya, clinging to which the being lost their (deen) faith — that is, dharma — that Maya went with no one at the end.
3QQT: Paai = on the foot. Gaafil = the heedless (person). ||13||
(So) the careless person struck their own foot with an axe by their own hand (that is, did themselves harm). ||13||
The idiot strikes his own foot with the axe by his own hand. ||13||
Thus, the ignorant man has struck his foot with an exe by his own hand.

The being, heedless of the Name, has struck the axe of greed on the foot of the intellect with their own hand. ||13|| ☬ Sri Kabir ji came back from bathing in the Ganga, and some day's festival was going on in Kashi. Someone said, "You too should see the show." To that Sri Kabir ji says; or: Ramanand ji had a show staged in Kashi to test him, and at that time said to Kabir ji, "Have you seen it?"
ZJ25: Jah jah = wherever. Hau = I. Kautak = shows, spectacles. Thao thaai = in place after place, in every place.
O Kabir! Wherever I have gone, in place after place (I have seen) only the shows of 'dunia' (the world);
Kabeer, wherever I go, I see wonders everywhere.
Kabir, wherever I went, I saw wonderful plays everywhere,
O brother — or, O Guru! Wherever I have wandered, in each of those places I have seen (kautak) shows going on.
MUAU: Sanehee = one who loves. Baahra = without. Oojar = a wilderness. Merai bhaai = in my view. Ram sanehee = one who loves Ram, a lover of Parmatma. ||14||
but in my view the place where there is no lover of Parmatma (no saint) is a wilderness (because there I saw only 'dunia' and no trace of 'deen'). ||14||
But without the devotees of the One Lord, it is all wilderness to me. ||14||
however, without the devotees of the Lord, the world is a wilderness for me.
But without the One — the saints who love Ram — that place is like a wilderness to my (bhaai) mind, or in my feeling; meaning, it is fearsome. ||14||
4RQY: Jhungeea = a tiny hut, a poor little shack. Bhalee = beautiful. Bhath = (like) a furnace. Gaau = village. Kustee = dishonest, false person.

O Kabir! Even the poor little hut of the saints is beautiful (to me) (there 'deen' is traded), but the village of a false person is like a (burning) furnace (there the fire of craving for 'dunia' burns at every moment).
Kabeer, the dwelling of the Saints is good; the dwelling of the unrighteous burns like an oven.
Kabir, blessed is the tenement of the saint; the abode of the sinners burns like a furnace.

Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, even the (jhungeea) grass hut of the saints is good — meaning, in it the mind finds peace — and even the village of a (kustee) stubborn, false person is scorching like a furnace.
H8CC: Aag = fire (a future imperative, third person, singular, as the words 'bhijau' and 'varsau' in "bhijau sijau kamblee, Alah varsau meh"). Tih dhaulhar = that mansion. Jih = in which (mansion). Ko = of. Naau = the Name. ||15||
Let the mansion in which Parmatma's Name is not remembered catch fire (I have no need of such mansions). ||15||
Those mansions in which the Lord's Name is not chanted might just as well burn down. ||15||
Let fire prey upon those mansions, in which the Name of God is not.

So let that (dhaulhar) mansion too catch fire in which Hari's Name is not uttered; meaning, without the Name it is fruitless. ||15|| ☬ Seeing people weeping at the death of a saint, he speaks for their sake:
CHCM: Kia roeeai = no need to weep; why weep? Grih = into the home. Apune grih = into one's own home, that home which is wholly one's own, from which no one will drive one out. Jaai = goes.

O Kabir! There is no need to grieve at the death of a saint, because that saint goes into the home from which no one will drive them out (that is, being a trader in 'deen', that saint reaches Prabhu's feet);
Kabeer, why cry at the death of a Saint? He is just going back to his home.
Kabir why wail at the death of a saint? He is merely going to his own Home.

Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, the one who goes into their own (grih) true form — meaning, that saint, giving up the body, attains the state beyond limiting conditions — one should not weep for their giving up the body.
9CKZ: Saakat = one cut off from God, a being separated from Parmatma, who is losing 'deen' for the sake of 'dunia'. Baapura = poor, unfortunate, wretched. Rovahu = grieve. Ju = who. Haattai haat = from shop to shop, at every shop, from one shop to another. Bikaai = is sold, is sent round in exchange for the vices committed. ||16||

(If you must grieve, then) grieve for (the death of) that wretched one who is separated from Prabhu's feet; (in exchange for their own evil deeds) they are sold at every shop (that is, having wandered for 'dunia' all their life, they now wander through many births). ||16||
Cry for the wretched, faithless cynic, who is sold from store to store. ||16||
Weep you for the wretched mammon-worshipper who is sold from shop to ship.
So one should weep for the wretched saakat, because on dying they are sold from shop to shop; meaning, taking countless births in the 8.4 million, they keep wandering. ||16||
HA3P: Saakat = a person cut off from Prabhu, one who loses 'deen' for the sake of 'dunia'. Lasan = garlic. Khaan = storeroom, store.
O Kabir! Think of the person who is cut off from God (who keeps losing 'deen' for the sake of 'dunia') as a storeroom full of garlic.
Kabeer, the faithless cynic is like a piece of garlic.
Kabir, as is the piece of garlic, so is an infidel.
Sri Kabir ji says: the saakat is like a (khaan) chutney of garlic.
6D38: Konai = in the corner (of some house), in some hidden place. Baithe = baith, sitting. Pargat hoe = comes out, becomes known. Nidaan = in the end, at last, surely. ||17||
Even if garlic is eaten sitting in some hidden place, it surely comes out (by its smell) (from within the saakat too, whenever words come out, they will be bad words). ||17||
Even if you eat it sitting in a corner, it becomes obvious to everyone. ||17||
Even if one eats it sitting in a corner, it becomes manifest at last.

Even if it is eaten sitting in a lonely (kone) corner, its stench (nidaan) in the end comes out. In the same way, through the company of the saakat the stench of engaging in evil deeds spreads; so one should not keep company with a saakat. ||17||
8FJK: Maaia = 'dunia'. Dolnee = churning pot, pot of milk. Pavan = air, breath. Jhakolanhaar = the thing with which milk is churned, the churning stick.
O Kabir! Think of this 'dunia' (this Maya) as a pot full of milk; take (every being's) every breath as the churning stick (for churning that pot).
Kabeer, Maya is the butter-churn, and the breath is the churning-stick.
Kabir wealth is the churning pot and the breath is the churning staff.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this body, made of Maya, is a (dolnee) churning pot; in it is the churning stick of the breaths, which are wind.
JD7K: Santahu = the saints, those people who do not let 'deen' be lost for the sake of 'dunia'. Chhaachh = buttermilk. Sansaar = the trader in 'dunia'. ||18||

(Those who learned the art of churning this milk, who used this Maya while remembering Parmatma, who traded in 'dunia' but did not let 'deen' be lost —) those saints (obtained) butter (from this churning) and ate it (that is, they gained the true purpose of human birth, as the purpose of churning milk is to draw out butter); but the trader in 'dunia' alone is (as it were) only drinking buttermilk (has not gained the true purpose of human birth). ||18||
The Saints eat the butter, while the world drinks the whey. ||18||
The saints eat the butter and the world drinks the butter-milk.
The saints, reflecting on the true and the untrue, have eaten the butter of the knowledge of their own true form; and the beings of the world drink only the buttermilk of untrue things. ||18||
LFHZ: Vahai = moves. Hiv = snow. Hivdhaar = snow-cold, cool, calm. Pavan = breath. Pavan hivdhaar vahai = (in the pot in which) the churning stick of calm breaths moves, the churning stick of breaths cooled by the Name stirs.
O Kabir! This 'dunia' (Maya) is, as it were, a pot of milk; (in this pot) breaths with the coolness (of the Name) are, as it were, the churning stick being stirred.
Kabeer, Maya is the butter-churn; the breath flows like ice water.
Kabir, mammonish body is the churning-pot in which breath flows like the stream of iced water.

Sri Kabir ji says: in the churning pot of the body made of Maya, the breaths of the reflective person (vahai) move as cool as a stream of (hiv) snow; meaning, they are free of attachment and aversion.
J24S: Jin = the person who. Biloia = has churned (with this churning stick). Avar = other people. Bilovanhaar = are only churning. ||19||

The (fortunate person) who has churned (the milk with this churning stick) has eaten (the butter); the others are only churning (they do not get butter to eat). (That is, those who use Maya only for their livelihood, and alongside keep remembering Parmatma with every breath, have lives full of peace; they gain the true purpose of human birth. But those who, forgetting 'deen', run after 'dunia' alone are ruined and waste their life.) ||19||
Whoever does the churning eats the butter; the others are just churning-sticks. ||19||
Whosoever churns, he eats the butter. Others, like the churning-rod obtain nothing.
The reflective people who have reflected have eaten the butter of the essence of the self; and the seekers are still at the churning of reflection. ||19||
F5VW: Chortee = (from the word 'chor', 'chorta' is a masculine diminutive noun; 'chortee' is its feminine) a wretched little thief, a cheat, a sweet-talking swindler. Mus = cheating. Mus mus = cheating again and again. Laavai haat = sets up shop.
O Kabir! This world, this Maya, is a sweet-talking swindler; cheating and cheating (those who, forgetting 'deen', wander for 'dunia' alone), this Maya keeps decking out her shop (more and more).
Kabeer, Maya is the thief, which breaks in and plunders the store.
Kabir, mammon, is a thief, who breaks into and plunders the shop.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this Maya is a thief who, (mus mus) enchanting and enchanting beings, sets them in the shops of the senses.
DGGH: Na musai = is not cheated. Jin = the one who. Baarah baat = twelve pieces, twelve parts. ||20||
O Kabir! Only that person escapes her swindling who has cut this Maya into twelve pieces (who has smashed her swindling). ||20||
Only Kabeer is not plundered; he has cut her into twelve pieces. ||20||
Kabir alone is plundered not, He is the one who has cut it into twelve pieces.

From this Maya only one (kabira) great-souled saint is not robbed — the one who has sent her down twelve (baat) roads; meaning, who has shared it out to the poor; or, who has sent it out on the road from the outside, that is, has not hoarded it; or, those who have (baarah baat) met with hardship. ||20||
KZ3H: Enh jug = in this human birth, having gained this human birth. Karahi ju = which you are making. Bahutai meet = many friends (here a son, there a wife, here wealth, there kingdom and fortune).
O Kabir! (Forgetting 'deen', forgetting Parmatma,) you are making many friends (son, wife, wealth, estate and the like); in this human birth you will not find peace (from these friends).
Kabeer, peace does not come in this world by making lots of friends.
Kabir, making good many friends alone, one does not attain peace in this world.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, the people who, in this Kali Yuga — that is, in the world — make many friends do not find peace.
BL53: Ek siu = with the One Parmatma. Raakhahi = keep joined. Te = those people. ||21||
Only those people always enjoy peace who (even while dealing in 'dunia') keep their mind joined to the One Parmatma. ||21||
Those who keep their consciousness focused on the One Lord shall find eternal peace. ||21||
They, who keep their mind fixed on One God, ever attain to peace.
The people who, knowing the One Vahiguru alone to be their supreme friend, keep their mind on Him — those people find peace every day. ||21||
9PU4: Marne te = from dying; from the death of breaking attachment to son, wife, wealth, estate and the like; from dying to attachment to 'dunia'; from breaking attachment with 'dunia'. Jag darai = the world fears, the world shrinks back, the world hesitates. Aanand = joy.

(Forgetting 'deen' for the sake of 'dunia', a person makes many friends — wealth, son, wife and the like — and hopes for comfort from them; because of this hope he cannot break attachment to them. But) O Kabir! The death (of giving up attachment) from which the world shrinks back brings joy to my mind;
Kabeer, the world is afraid of death - that death fills my mind with bliss.
Kabir, death, of which the world is terrified, is pleasing to my mind;
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, the dying from which the world is afraid — through that dying there is bliss in my mind.
38WA: Marne hee te = only by breaking attachment to the many friends, son and the rest. Parmaanand = the Parmatma in whom is supreme bliss, the Prabhu who is Master of the highest joy. ||22||
Only by dying to this attachment to 'dunia' is that Parmatma found who is perfect bliss itself. ||22||
It is only by death that perfect, supreme bliss is obtained. ||22||
it is in death alone, that one is blessed with the perfect supreme bliss.
For only by dying is perfect supreme bliss gained; meaning, the spiritually wise, giving up the body, gain the happiness of bodiless liberation and become one with Braham. ||22||
FS27: Padaarath = beautiful thing. Paai kai = having gained, if you have found.

(Wherever you look, there is running about for 'dunia' alone; so) O Kabir! If (by good fortune) you have found the beautiful thing that is Parmatma's Name, do not go opening this bundle before others.
The Treasure of the Lord is obtained, O Kabeer, but do not undo its knot.
Attaining to the Lord's treasures, O Kabir, open you not its knot.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, having gained the treasure that is Ram's Name, do not open the knot; meaning, do not teach one who is not qualified.
U1L7: Pattan = city. Paarkhoo = tester, one who knows the worth. Gaahak = buyer. Mol = the price of giving up attachment to 'dunia' ('it is gained only by dying'). ||23||

(The world is so drunk on 'dunia' that, to buy the treasure of the Name,) there is neither a market, nor anyone who values this thing, nor anyone who wants to buy it, nor anyone ready to pay such a price (as breaking love with 'dunia'). ||23||
There is no market to sell it, no appraiser, no customer, and no price. ||23||
There is no city to sell it, no assayer, no customer and no price for it.
Where there is no (pattan) city of the true company, no tester who knows reality, no buyer who is a seeker, and no price of faith. ||23||
MRHG: Ta siu = with that (member of the holy company). Ja ko = whose (support and refuge). Thaakur = sustainer.
O Kabir! Form a bond with that (member of the holy company) whose (support and refuge) is Parmatma, the Sustainer of all (love formed with the traders in the 'treasure of Ram' lasts to the end;
Kabeer, be in love with only that one, whose Master is the Lord.
Kabir, profess you love for him alone whose Master is the Lord.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, love those saints whose Thakur is Ram alone. Meaning, the saints trust in no one but Vahiguru.
J9QC: Bhoopat = (bhoo = earth; pati = master) landowners, kings. Kaune kaam aavahi = of what use are they? Of no use; they do not keep company to the end. ||24||
but those who are proud of learning, kingdom, land and the like, who are traders in 'dunia' —) whether pandits, or kings, or masters of great lands, they are of no use. ||24||
The Pandits, the religious scholars, kings and landlords - what good is love for them? ||24||
The scholars, kings and the landlords, of what avail is love for them?

Pandits and kings who are masters of the earth — of what use will they be through loving them? That is, of no use. Meaning, they are no help in the next world. ||24|| ☬ Question: what is the gain in loving the One?
GS8X: Aan = other, of 'dunia'. Dubidha = double-mindedness, dread. Jaai = goes away.
O Kabir! The other dreads (of 'dunia') go away only if love is formed with the One Parmatma.
Kabeer, when you are in love with the One Lord, duality and alienation depart.
O Kabir, the worldly love departs by loving the One Lord.
Sri Kabir ji says: by loving the One, the (dubidha) sense of duality, which makes the being separate from Parmeshvar, goes away. ☬ And as long as the sense of duality has not gone —
5UHU: Bhaavai = whether. Laanbe kes kar = grow matted locks (smearing ashes) (and leaving 'dunia', go and camp outside). Gharar mudaai = shave the head completely, become a clean-shaven sadhu and give up 'dunia'. Keeai = if it is done. ||25||

(As long as love is not joined with Prabhu, the dread of 'dunia' cannot be wiped away,) whether you keep long matted locks (smeared with ash), or shave your head completely (and go and camp in forests or at pilgrimage places). ||25||
You may have long hair, or you may shave your head bald. ||25||
It matters not, whether you wear long hair or whether you shave your head clean.

whether one grows long hair, matted locks and the like, or (gharar) scrapes it off and shaves — that is, becomes a paramhans — meaning, both their deeds are useless. Or: by loving the One, one (bidha) merges into His bliss — that is, becomes one with Him. Then, whether one keeps long hair — that is, stays engaged in the world — or shaves the head — meaning, gives up everything — there is no further loss or gain for them. ||25||
PNSY: Jag = the world, attachment to 'dunia'. Andh = blind people, those who have no understanding of 'deen', whose eyes are not opened. Tis mah = into that room (where the soot of attachment to 'dunia' is). Kaajal = soot.

O Kabir! Attachment to 'dunia' is, as it were, a room full of soot; into it have fallen the people whose eyes are closed (who have not gained understanding of 'deen', whether they are pandits, kings or landowners, or renunciants such as matted-haired sannyasis).
Kabeer, the world is a room filled with black soot; the blind fall into its trap.
Kabir, the world is but a black chamber of the lamp-soot. The blind ones alone fall into its trap.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this world is a room of the soot of sins; in it lie beings blind through ignorance.
VED7: Balihaaree = a sacrifice. Hau = I. Pais = entering, falling in, dwelling. Neekas jaahi = come out. ||26||
But I am a sacrifice to those who fall into it and come out again (who, forming love with the One Parmatma, give up attachment to 'dunia'). ||26||
I am a sacrifice to those who are thrown in, and still escape. ||26||
I am a sacrifice to those, who even when cast into it, escape unsoiled.
I am a sacrifice to those who, falling into this room, come out again. Meaning, the saints who, taking birth in the world, become sinless again and merge into Vahiguru are blessed. ||26||
ULU1: Jaaiga = will perish. Sakahu = if you can (stop it), if you can prevent it from perishing. Ta = then. Lehu bahor = stop it, save it.
O Kabir! This whole body will perish; if you can save it from perishing, save it (that is, no one can save their body from perishing; it will surely perish).
Kabeer, this body shall perish; save it, if you can.
Kabir this body must perish; if you can, then save it.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this body will surely perish; if you are able, turn it back — that is, make it fruitful by remembering Hari.
BAVM: Te = those people. Naange paavahu = barefoot, just like paupers. Jin ke = with whom. ||27||

The people who had hundreds of thousands and tens of millions of rupees stored up also went from here barefoot (that is, like paupers) (all their life they wandered for 'dunia' and forgot 'deen'; in the end this 'dunia' stayed here, and they left utterly bankrupt in spiritual life). ||27||
Even those who have tens of thousands and millions, must depart bare-footed in the end. ||27||
Even they, have to depart barefooted who has amassed millions and millions.
For those who had hundreds of thousands and tens of millions in hand — that is, great rich men or kings — they too went barefoot at the end. ||27||
4QRU: Kavnai maarag = on some road, to some task, to some work that is profitable.
O Kabir! This body will perish; put it to some (such) work (as is profitable for you);
Kabeer, this body shall perish; place it on the path.
Kabir, when this body has to depart, then put it on the good path.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this body will surely go at the end — meaning, will die — so set it on some road. ☬ What road?
BXT8: so, keep the holy company and sing Prabhu's praise ('dunia' stays right here; only 'deen' becomes one's companion). ||28||
Either join the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, or sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord. ||28||
Either, associate you with the saints, or sing you your God's praises.
Either keep the company of the saints or sing Hari's virtues; meaning, setting this body on the good road, make it fruitful. ||28||
KTRC: Marta marta = dying again and again, dying day after day, pressed down each day by the dread of death. Mar na jaania = did not learn the way of dying (to the dread of death), did not learn the way to end the dread of death. Aise marne jo marai = the one who dies to Maya in this way (as told in salok 28 above), who dies to Maya by singing Prabhu's praise in the holy company.
O Kabir! The world (the trader in 'dunia' alone) stays pressed down every moment by the dread of death; no one (who trades in Maya alone) understands how this dread of death is to be ended.
Kabeer, dying, dying, the whole world has to die, and yet, none know how to die.
Kabir, dying, by one's turn, everyone has to die, and yet, none knows how to die.
Sri Kabir ji says: dying and dying, the whole world has died; but no one has known dying while living.

LUZR: Bahur = again and again. Bahur na marna hoe = they do not again and again have the dread of death. ||29||
The person who dies while living (breaks attachment to 'dunia') (by singing Prabhu's praise in the holy company) no longer has this dread. ||29||
Let those who die, die such a death, that they shall never have to die again. ||29||
Whosoever dies, let him die such a death, that he may not have to die again.
Those who have died the (marne) death of giving up the sense of self while living — those with such a death do not again undergo birth and death; meaning, they become the form of liberation. ||29||
SWE6: Maanas = human. Baarai baar = again and again.
O Kabir! Human birth is gained with great difficulty, (and if, forgetting Prabhu's Name and absorbed only in 'dunia', it slips from the hand once,) it is not gained again and again;
Kabeer, it is so difficult to obtain this human body; it does not just come over and over again.
Kabir, difficult to obtain is the human birth, it comes not again and again,
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, this human birth is very rare; it is not gained again and again.
3PW6: Ban = forest. Paake = ripe. Bhui = on the ground. Girahi = fall. Daar = branch. ||30||
just as, (when) the ripe fruit of the forest trees fall to the ground, they do not attach to the branch again. ||30||
It is like the ripe fruit on the tree; when it falls to the ground, it cannot be re-attached to the branch. ||30||
just as the ripe fruit of the forest, which when falls to the ground, attaches not again to the branch.

Just as fruit in the forest, ripening, falls from the trees to the earth, and having fallen can never attach again to that same branch; meaning, do not waste this excellent body. ||30|| ☬ A seeker, hearing of Sri Kabir ji's fame, came to him and asked, "Is your name Kabir?" Then Kabir ji said, "Brother, what is your purpose?" He said, "That I may meet Ram, and that you may do me good." Then, knowing him to be highly qualified, he gives the essential teaching:
8Y3N: Tuhee too = You, You alone, only You. Kabir = the greatest of all.

(The true purpose of this human birth is 'gaining Parmatma's Name'; for this it is necessary that Parmatma be remembered and Prabhu's virtues be sung; so) O Kabir! (Always say: O Prabhu!) You alone are the greatest of all; Your Name alone is the greatest of all.
Kabeer, you are Kabeer; your name means great.
O my God, You Yourself is great God and great is Your Name.
In the past too, You alone were Parmeshvar, (kabira) greater than all; and now too You alone are the form of Hari, (kabir) greater than all; in the future too Your Name alone will be great.
DYWV: Tajahi = if (O Kabir) you give up. Sareer = attachment to the body, the dread of death, identification with the body. ||31||
(But along with this praise, O Kabir,) only if you first give up attachment to your body is the jewel of Parmatma's Name found. ||31||
O Lord, You are Kabeer. The Jewel of the Lord is obtained, when the mortal first gives up his body. ||31||
When man first abandons his bodily ego, then alone, obtains he the Lord's jewel.
O brother! When the being first gives up pride in this body, then the jewel that is Ram is attained. ||31|| ☬ Someone said, "By the power of wealth I will make it so." For that one:
W5BD: Jhankh = grumbling, complaints. Na hoe = cannot happen.
O Kabir! (The meaning of 'giving up the body' is that) we should not keep grumbling (for the sake of 'dunia'); what you say (caught in greed for 'dunia') cannot simply happen,
Kabeer, do not struggle in stubborn pride; nothing happens just because you say so.
Kabir, prate you not in vain. Nothing shall happen at your bidding.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, do not (jhankeeai) babble on like this in ego. Meaning, do not ruin yourself, because what you say never simply happens.
27N6: Karam = grace. Kareem = the gracious Prabhu ji. Met na saakai = cannot increase or decrease. ||32||
(Along with singing His praise, also keep faith that) the gifts the gracious Prabhu ji gives (to beings) cannot be increased or decreased by anyone (else). ||32||
No one can erase the actions of the Merciful Lord. ||32||
No one can set aside the deed, which the Merciful Master is doing.
The deeds that Vahiguru ji, the doer of (karam) grace, is doing — no one can wipe them out. ||32||
8JFW: Kash = (Sanskrit kash, to test, rub on a touchstone) to test, to rub on a stone, as gold is rubbed to test it. Vatee = (Sanskrit vata) a small stone. Kas vatee = the stone on which gold is rubbed to test whether it is true or false. Kasautee = kas-vattee, touchstone. Kasautee Ram kee = the touchstone by which a person's true love for Prabhu can be tested. Jhootha = one who loves falsehood, who is attached to 'dunia' alone, who loses 'deen' for the sake of 'dunia'. Sahai = bears, passes, proves true. Mar jeeva = one who has died and lives again, who has died to 'dunia' and come alive to 'deen', who has ended identification with the body. Na tikai = does not prove true in the test, does not pass.
O Kabir! The person who is attached to 'dunia' does not prove true on the touchstone by which a person's true love for Prabhu is tested.
Kabeer, no one who is false can withstand the Touchstone of the Lord.
Kabir, no one, who is false, can withstand the Lord's touchstone.
Sri Kabir ji says: coming into the true company, chanting and austerity are Ram's touchstone; so before it no one false can stand, except the highly qualified.
8ZV4: Only that person passes the test of love for Prabhu who has died to attachment to 'dunia' and come alive in the love of 'deen'. ||33||
He alone can pass the test of the Lord's Touchstone, who remains dead while yet alive. ||33||
He alone can bear the Lord's ordeal, one who remains dead in life.
Only that excellent person bears this touchstone of Ram who has died to the sense of self; meaning, who has given up pride in the body. ||33||
045K: Oojal = bright, clean, white, fine. Pahirahi = wear. Kaapre = clothes. Khaahi = eat. Paan supaaree khaahi = eat betel and areca to look smart and handsome.
O Kabir! (The traders in 'dunia' alone, for their own show,) wear fine clothes and eat betel and areca;
Kabeer, some wear gaudy robes, and chew betel leaves and betel nuts.
Kabir, men wear gaudy robes and eat betal-leaves and betal-nuts.
Sri Kabir ji says: the people who wear (oojal) white clothes and eat rolls of betel and areca — meaning, who enjoy the pleasures of the senses —
EPAU: Baadhe = bound, bound in attachment to adorning the body. Jampur = in the city of Yama, under Yama's control, under Yama's pressure, in the dread of death. Jaanhi = go, stay settled. ||34||

but those people, bound (by attachment to adorning the body), stay settled in the dread of death and the like, because they remain without Parmatma's Name (attachment to 'dunia', forgetting 'deen', is painful in every state). ||34||
Without the Name of the One Lord, they are bound and gagged and taken to the City of Death. ||34||
However, without the Name of One God, they are bound and marched off to the Yama's city.
those people, without chanting the Name of the One Hari, at the end go to the city of Yama, bound by Yama's messengers; meaning, they will come to hells. ||34||
XYB4: Berra = ship. Jarjara = very old, rotten, worm-eaten. Phoote = burst, have opened. Chhenk hajaar = thousands of holes.
O Kabir! If a ship is very old, with thousands of holes burst open in it,
Kabeer, the boat is old, and it has thousands of holes.
Kabir, old is the boat and thousands of holes have appeared in it.

Sri Kabir ji says: this ship of the body is (jarjara) old — that is, it has come to decay — and thousands of holes of sensual vices have opened in it. Meaning, through those holes the water of sins keeps coming in, and with it the ship grows heavy.
V5EW: Harooe harooe = light, lightly laden, those who have not taken on a load. Tir gae = cross over. ||35||

(it will surely sink in the sea in the end; of this ship's passengers) only those people cross over who have not taken on any load; but those on whose heads there is a load drown (pressed down under the load). ||35||
Those who are light get across, while those who carry the weight of their sins on their heads are drowned. ||35||
They, who are light of weight (without the wheavy weight of sins) cross over and those with heavy load (of sins) on their head are drowned.

Those who, having gained this ship of the body, are free of the load of pride in the body or in their qualities — that is, are light — have crossed this ocean of the world; that is, have become the form of well-being. And those on whose heads was the load of body-pride or of sins have drowned; meaning, they will keep being born and dying. ||35||
2N8S: (Forgetting 'deen' and running about for 'dunia' alone, a person gets so caught in attachment to their body that they live every moment in dread of death. Yet this body cannot last for ever; death does come; then) O Kabir! (When the body is laid on the pyre) the bones burn like wood, the hair burns like grass.
Kabeer, the bones burn like wood, and the hair burns like straw.
Kabir, the bones burn like wood and the hair burn like grass.
Sri Kabir ji says: when a person dies, the bones burn just as wood burns, and the hair burns like grass.
WZCG: Udaas = detached, unattached (from attachment to the body made of bones, hair and the like). ||36||

Seeing this whole world burning (that is, seeing that all beings are in the end surely separated from this body), I, Kabir, have become detached from attachment to this body (I have given up attachment to the body). ||36||
Seeing the world burning like this, Kabeer has become sad. ||36||
Seeing this world on fire like this, Kabir has become sad.
Seeing the beings of this world burning in this way, our mind has become (kabir) greatly detached from this world. ||36||
G4R6: O Kabir! One should not take pride (in the youth, beauty and the like of this body); (in the end it is only) (a handful of) bones wrapped in skin.
Kabeer, do not be so proud of your bones wrapped up in skin.
Kabir, take not you pride on your bones wrapped up in skin.
Sri Kabir ji says: do not take pride in your body, because in it are only bones, wrapped in skin; meaning, it is filled with bones, flesh, blood, excrement, urine and the like.
F9P4: Haivar = hai-var, haya-var, choice fine horses. Var = choice, fine. Chhatr = canopy. Tar = under, beneath. Te phun = those people too, such people too. Dharnee = earth, soil. Gaad = mix, blend in. ||37||
Those people too (who took pride in this body) in the end mixed with the dust, who (rode) on fine horses and sat under (waving) canopies. ||37||
Those who were on their horses and under their canopies, were eventually buried under the ground. ||37||
They, who were on the horses and under the canopies, were at last buried under the earth.
The people who rode on (haivar) the best horses and went under a canopy — that is, who ruled as kings — those people too were buried in the earth at the end. ||37||
DZ5Q: O Kabir! One should not take pride (either) on seeing one's own lofty mansion (this too is a game of a few days;
Kabeer, do not be so proud of your tall mansions.
Kabir, be you not proud on seeing yours lofty mansions.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, do not take pride on seeing your (avaas) house high.
6RBK: Aaj kaalh = today or tomorrow, very soon. Bhui = on the ground, on the earth. Jaamai = grows. ||38||
when death comes, leaving this mansion,) today or tomorrow we must mix with the dust; grass will grow over our (body). ||38||
Today or tomorrow, you shall lie beneath the ground, and the grass shall grow above you. ||38||
Today or tomorrow you shall lie beneath the earth and grass shall grow over you.
For today or tomorrow, on dying, this body will lie on the earth, and again grass will grow over it; meaning, having died it will become dust. ||38||
E8US: O Kabir! (If you are wealthy,) do not take pride (in this wealth either), nor mock any pauper (you see).
Kabeer, do not be so proud, and do not laugh at the poor.
Kabir! Let no one take pride or laugh at the poor.
Sri Kabir ji says: having gained splendour, do not be proud, and do not laugh at (koe) any (rank) poor person, blind person or other helpless one.
T1AK: Naau = boat, the boat of life. Kia jaanau = what do I know? Na haseeai = do not mock. ||39||
(Your own life-) boat is still at sea; no one knows what may happen (it takes no time for this wealth to slip from the hand). ||39||
Your boat is still out at sea; who knows what will happen? ||39||
As yet the boat is in the sea. Who knows what may happen?
For the boat of the body is still in the ocean of the world. Who knows what will become of us; meaning, stay in awe. ||39||
0LBC: Dehee = body. Surang = of beautiful colour.
O Kabir! One should not take pride even on seeing this body of beautiful colour;
Kabeer, do not be so proud, looking at your beautiful body.
Kabir, be not proud on seeing your beauteous body.
Sri Kabir ji says: do not take pride on seeing your body of beautiful colour — that is, seeing yourself beautiful.
RJRG: Aaj kaalh = today or tomorrow, in a little while. Kaanchuree = slough, cast-off skin. Bhuyang = snake. ||40||
you will leave this body too in a few days, as a snake sheds its skin (the soul and the body too have no firm, lasting partnership). ||40||
Today or tomorrow, you will have to leave it behind, like the snake shedding its skin. ||40||
You shall leave it today or tomorrow as a serpent does its slough.
For you will leave this beautiful body today or tomorrow and go, just as a snake leaves its (kaanchuree) skin. ||40||
UGPU: Lootna hai = if you want to gather it up in heaps, if you want to collect it. Ta = then. Loot lai = gather it. Ram naam hai loot = Parmatma's Name is being given away freely, Prabhu's Name is being handed out in heaps.
O Kabir! (Why are you wandering for 'dunia'? See,) Parmatma's Name is being handed out in heaps; if you want to gather something, gather this wealth of the Name.
Kabeer, if you must rob and plunder, then plunder the plunder of the Lord's Name.
Kabir, if you can plunder, then you must plunder the loot of the Lord's Name.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, if you want to plunder, then make the effort and plunder the loot that is Ram's Name.
KJB1: Phir = again, when the time has passed. ||41||
When the soul has left (the body), when the time has passed, you will have to regret it. ||41||
Otherwise, in the world hereafter, you will regret and repent, when the breath of life leaves the body. ||41||
Otherwise, you shall afterwards repent when your soul shall leave the body.
Otherwise, when your breath of life departs, then you will only repent afterwards; meaning, without the Name you will waste your life. ||41||
U5FY: Koee na janmio = only a rare one is (born). Apnai...aag = who sets fire to their own house, who burns their sense of "mine", who ends identification with the body.
(But to gather the wealth of the Name it is necessary that a person first end the sense of "mine", and) O Kabir! Only a rare one is found (in the world) who burns their attachment to the body,
Kabeer, there is no one born, who burns his own home,
Kabir, there is not even a single such man, who applies fire to his own home,
Sri Kabir ji says: no such one has been born — meaning, only a rare one has been born — who kindles in their own heart the fire of seeing everything as Braham,
PP7Q: Paanchau larika = the five boys, the five sons of Maya, lust and the rest. Jaar kai = burning. Laag rahai = keeps joined. Liv = the thread of attention. ||42||
and, burning all five sons of Maya, lust and the rest, keeps their attention joined to (the remembrance of) Parmatma. ||42||
and burning his five sons, remains lovingly attuned to the Lord. ||42||
and who by burning his five sons, remains attuned to the Lord alone.
and, burning the five boys, lust, anger and the rest, with that fire, keeps the mind fixed on the One Name of Ram alone. ||42||
K90W: Larika = 'the five boys', the five sons of Maya, lust and the rest. Larikee = girls, Maya's daughters, hope, craving, envy and the like. Bechai = gives in exchange for the wealth of the Name; to buy the wealth of the Name, gives up these, lust and the rest, and hope, craving and the rest. Ko hai = only a rare one is. Bechaee = bechai, sells.

Only a rare one trades (in His Name) with Parmatma, who gives (the five) sons (of Maya, lust and the rest) and (her) daughters (hope, craving, envy and the like) in exchange (to buy the wealth of the Name).
Kabeer, how rare are those who sell their son and sell their daughter
Kabir is there such a one, who sells off his son and sells off daughter,

Sri Kabir ji says: whoever sells the boy that is the mind — that is, offers the mind to the Guru — to them the Guru gives the (larkee) knowledge of Braham; or, whoever gives the intellect, to them the Guru gives spiritual knowledge.
DJXV: Saajha = partnership, partnership in the true company, partnership in trading the wealth of the Name. Kabir siu = with Kabir; Kabir wishes it were with me. Har sang banaj = trading in Hari's Name by giving the 'boys and girls' to Hari. Banaj = deal, exchange, trade. ||43||
Kabir wishes that such a person would form a partnership of the true company with me too (in this trade). ||43||
and, entering into partnership with Kabeer, deal with the Lord. ||43||
and entering into partnership with Kabir, deals with his God alone?
In this way, whoever forms a partnership with the saints, (kabir) greatest of all, then trades with Hari in the form of oneness. ||43||
8882: Chetaavnee = reminder, warning. Mat = lest, in case. Sahsa = regret, longing, doubt.
O Kabir! I am reminding you, lest regret remain afterwards;
Kabeer, let me remind you of this. Do not be skeptical or cynical.
Kabir, I remind you of it, Live you not under any doubt.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, we have given you this warning — that is, reminded you — lest doubt remain in your mind; meaning, having gained this birth, be free of doubt.
S1BW: Paachhai = in life up till now. Bhog ju = the pleasures that. Paachhai bhog ju bhogve = the pleasures enjoyed up till now. Tin ko = in exchange for those pleasures. Tin ko gurr lai khaahi = (the worth of those pleasures is only so much that) you might take a little jaggery for them and eat it; in return for them only a little jaggery can be had (as a customer who buys goods at a shop asks for a little jaggery afterwards as a small extra). ||44||

The pleasures you have enjoyed up till now (lest you think you have had a great time — in truth) are worth only so much (as when, buying goods at a shop, one takes as a small extra) a little jaggery and eats it. ||44||
Those pleasures which you enjoyed so much in the past - now you must eat their fruits. ||44||
Now, you are eating the fruit of those deeds that you did in the past.
For the pleasures you enjoyed before, go take jaggery from some shopkeeper and eat it; meaning, nothing is gained from those pleasures. ||44||
WF2J: Jaanio = knew, had thought. Parribo bhalo = reading is good; the best work of human life is studying. Parribe siu = than reading. Jog = joining to Prabhu's feet.

O Kabir! (Seeing people of high castes here in Kashi studying the Vedas, Shastras and the like,) I had thought studying would be the best work of human birth; but (seeing these people's mere wrangling I have become convinced that) joining to Prabhu's feet is better (for a person) than studying (such learning).
Kabeer, at first, I thought learning was good; then I thought Yoga was better.
Kabir, firs, I thought learning to be good, then, I thought Yoga to be better.
Sri Kabir ji says: first I thought reading the Shastras good; then, after that, thinking yoga practices such as breath-control good, I practised yoga.
M3AX: Nindau = (future imperative, third person, singular) let them slander, let them call it bad. ||45||
(So,) though the world may call me bad for this, I will not give up devotion to Parmatma (even in exchange for learning). ||45||
I shall never abandon devotional worship of the Lord, even though people may slander me. ||45||
However, now I forsake not the Lord's adoration, though men may slander me.
Through yoga I did devotion; so now I will never give up devotion to Ram, even if people keep slandering me; meaning, I have known the taste and fruit of devotion to be above all. ||45||
K90J: Ki nindai = what can they slander? Who will accept the faults they find? Bapurra = poor wretch, fool. Jih man = in whose mind. Giaan = understanding, discernment of good and bad.
O Kabir! If a person who has no understanding (of how precious a gift devotion to Prabhu is, compared with learning, calls me bad for this choice of mine), that person's slander has no meaning.
Kabeer, how can the wretched people slander me? They have no wisdom or intelligence.
Kabir, how can the poor people, who have no gnosis in their mind, revile me?
Sri Kabir ji says: what will this (bapurra) poor crowd of people slander me with, since in their minds there is no knowledge of the true self or of devotion?
UR1F: Rav rahe = is remembering. Taje = taj, having given up. ||46||
So Kabir (does not care about the gossip of such people, and) is remembering Parmatma, and giving up attachment to all other (work). ||46||
Kabeer continues to dwell upon the Lord's Name; I have abandoned all other affairs. ||46||
Kabir continues to recite the Lord's name, abandoning all worldly affairs.
So now, giving up the schemes of other work, we are (rav rahe) chanting Ram alone, (kabir) greatest of all. ||46||
K9WK: Pardesee = this being, who has come to stay in this world for a few days like a traveller, as a yogi stops in some settlement for two or four days. Ghaaghra = (Sanskrit ghargar, a gate, a door) door (that is, a sense organ). Ghaaghrai = to the door, to the sense organ. Chahu dis = from all four sides (that is, to every sense organ). Aag = fire, the fire of vices (for the eyes, 'the vice of looking at others'; for the ears, slander of others; for the tongue, 'sweet taste', and so on).
The senses of this foreign being are on fire with vices on every side,
Kabeer, the robe of the stranger-soul has caught fire on all four sides.
Kabir, the stranger's petti-coat has caught fire on all the four sides.
Sri Kabir ji says: the (ghaaghrai) robe of the body of this foreign being has caught the fire of death from all four directions.
BSHG: Khintha = patched quilt, the quilt of the body of this foreign yogi. Taaga = the thread that holds the patches of this body-quilt together, the soul. Aanch = heat, the heat of the fire of vices. ||47||

(The yogi who, careless, kept enjoying the warmth of this fire —) his body-quilt burnt to coal (in the fire of vices); (but the foreign yogi who took care of this quilt's thread, the soul dwelling in this body, and kept shrinking from the taste of the warmth of the fire of vices —) his soul did not even feel the heat (of this fire of vices) (that is, he escaped this burning fire). ||47||
The cloth of the body has been burnt and reduced to charcoal, but the fire did not touch the thread of the soul. ||47||
The body has been burnt to charcoal, however, the fire has touched not the soul thread.
So the quilt that is the gross body has burnt to coal — that is, to ash — and the thread that is the subtle body, the soul-thread, or the self, does not even feel the heat. ||47||
19DR: Khaapar = the begging bowl in which the yogi begs flour from house to house; the mind that wanders from door to door, the mind that goes about ruined in many desires. Phoot maphoot = broken into pieces, began running after countless desires.
O Kabir! (The unfortunate being-yogi whose) body-quilt, falling into the fire of vices, burnt to coal, and (whose) mind-bowl kept gathering only the alms of desires from door to door —
Kabeer, the cloth has been burnt and reduced to charcoal, and the begging bowl is shattered into pieces.
Kabir the patched garment has been burnt and the begging bowl is completely shattered.

Sri Kabir ji says: the body that has arisen from the five elements — (khin) space, (tha) earth and (jal) water, (kuila) fire and the rest — is only a bowl. That bowl, which the being-yogi thought unbreakable, when it broke — that is, died —
1JRM: Bapurra = poor, unfortunate, who earned nothing in this round of birth. Khelio = wrecked the game, lost the game. Aasan = on the seat, in his lap. Bibhoot = ash, ruin. ||48||
that unfortunate being-yogi leaves having wrecked the game of human birth; only ash and ruin fall into his lap. ||48||
The poor Yogi has played out his game; only ashes remain on his seat. ||48||
The poor yogi has played his game, and on his seat remain but ashes.

then the poor being-yogi played for four days and went away. Afterwards the ash lay on his seat; meaning, on death, wealth and other splendour just lie there. Or: on the seat of the inner mind the ash of desire remained. Because of this the poor yogi went on to play in other bodies; meaning, the being under the sway of desire stays in the 8.4 million. ||48||

U5SB: Thorai jal = in a little water. Thorai jal maachhulee = a fish in a little water.

O Kabir! If a fish lives in a little water, the fisherman comes and casts his net (in the same way, if a being makes worldly pleasures, learning, wealth and the like the support of their life, the 'five boys' of Maya easily seize them).
Kabeer, the fish is in the shallow water; the fisherman has cast his net.
Kabir, the fish is in thin water and the fisherman casts his net.
Sri Kabir ji says: in the (thorai) meagre water of things, for this fish of the being, the fisherman Death has come and cast the net of dying.
4BZ1: Ih toghnai = in this hollow, in this pond, while dependent on these shallow supports. Samhaal = take care of, take hold of, take the support of. ||49||

O fish! Staying in this hollow you cannot escape the fisherman's net; if you want to escape, find the ocean (O soul! Making these pleasures your support, you cannot escape the blows of lust and the rest; leave these shallow supports and find Parmatma). ||49||
You shall not escape this little pool; think about returning to the ocean. ||49||
You shall escape not in this little pool, O fish. You ought to think of returning to the ocean again.

Even by these many efforts of serving other gods you will not escape from this water. So, O brother, (phir) turn back from this world and take hold of the ocean that is Vahiguru; meaning, by remembering the Name you will be free of the fear of death. ||49||
E8KS: O Kabir! One should not leave the ocean, even if (its water) is very salty;
Kabeer, do not leave the ocean, even if it is very salty.
Kabir, leave you not the ocean, though it be very saline.
Sri Kabir ji says: do not leave the ocean that is Parmeshvar, even if in it chanting, austerity and the like are very salty — that is, hard.
1KQA: Pokhar = (Sanskrit pushkar, a lake, a pond) pond. Pokhar = in a pond. Pokhar pokhar = in every pond. Pokhar pokhar dhoodhte = searching (for the soul's support) in little ponds. Koee na kahihai = no one says. ||50||
No one says it is a good thing to search in little ponds (for the soul's support). ||50||
If you poke around searching from puddle to puddle, no one will call you smart. ||50||
If you search for shelter from pond to pond, no one shall call you wise.
For, seeing those who leave the support of that Vahiguru and search for the (pokhar) ponds of gods and goddesses, or of pleasures, no good person will praise them. ||50||
V6QK: Gusaaeen = go-saaeen, Lord of the earth, the Prabhu-Master. Nigusaaeaa = without a master. Ni gusaaen = masterless. Bah gae = were swept away. Thaanghee = boatman, the Guru-boatman.
O Kabir! (This world is, as it were, an ocean across which the ships of beings' lives are passing; but) the ships that are masterless, on which there is no Guru-boatman, sink.
Kabeer, those who have no guru are washed away. No one can help them.
Kabir, they who have no Guru, are washed away. No one is a saviour of them.
Sri Kabir ji says: (nigusaaen) people without a Guru have been swept away in the ocean of the world; they have no (thaanghee) companion.
66VV: Deen = humility. Aapunee = (who made it) their own. Karte hoe su hoe = whatever happens from the Creator is (right); the Creator's will seems sweet to them. ||51||

The people who, (giving up their own cleverness,) taking on humility and lowliness, (have taken the support of the Guru-boatman), (seeing the waves of the world-ocean) remain carefree, knowing whatever happens to be the Creator's will (they have no worry about their ship sinking). ||51||
Be meek and humble; whatever happens is what the Creator Lord does. ||51||
Let you be resigned to your God in utter humility, and then let all that happen what the Creator does.
So, O brother, take on humility and lowliness on your own side, and on the Creator's side, let happen whatever the Creator does; meaning, stay happy in His will. ||51||
A9D7: Baisnau = a devotee of Parmatma. Kookar = bitch (kookar = dog). Saakat = a person cut off from God, the self-willed. Maai = mother. Buree = bad, unfortunate.
O Kabir! Know even the bitch of (some) devotee to be fortunate, but even the mother of a person cut off from God is unfortunate;
Kabeer, even the dog of a devotee is good, while the mother of the faithless cynic is bad.
Kabir, good is even the bitch of the Lord's sage and bad is the mother of an infidel.
Sri Kabir ji says: the bitch of the saints, devotees of Vishnu, is good, and the saakat's mother is bad.
WS6A: Oh = (this word is masculine; the word 'uh' is feminine) that devotee. Jas = glory. Bisaahan = buying. ||52||

because that devotee always sings the glory of Hari's Name, and in his company that bitch hears it too; (the saakat always earns sin; in his bad company) his mother too becomes a sharer in sins. ||52||
The dog hears the Praises of the Lord's Name, while the other is engaged in sin. ||52||
Become, the bitch hears God's Name and praise and the infidel's mother deals in sins.
For that bitch of the saints always hears the glory of Hari's Name, while the saakat's mother goes to (bisaahan) buy sins; so that bitch is the better. ||52||
HWS5: Doobla = thin, weak. Harna = the deer of the being. Ih = this world. Ih taal = this pond that is the world. Hareeaara = green, in which is the greenery of the pleasures of Maya.
O Kabir! This world is a pond in which there is endless greenery of the pleasures of Maya; this deer that is my soul is weak (it cannot keep from going towards this greenery).
Kabeer, the deer is weak, and the pool is lush with green vegetation.
Kabir, weak is the man-deer and this world tank is surrounded by verdure of temptations.
Sri Kabir ji says: in this pond of the world, with its greenery of sense-objects, this deer of the being wanders, grown thin.
8AG5: Aheree = hunters, endless vices. Ek = alone. Jeeu = being, soul. Keta kaal = how long a time? Not for long. Banchau = I can escape. ||53||
My soul is all alone; (to snare it, the pleasures of Maya are) hundreds of thousands of hunters; (by my own effort) I cannot escape (their blows) for long. ||53||
Thousands of hunters are chasing after the soul; how long can it escape death? ||53||
There are lakhs of hunters of one living being. How long can it escape death?
Hundreds of thousands of (aheree) hunters, the senses or desires, are out to kill it; so for how long will this one being escape them? That is, it cannot escape. ||53||
GMZS: Teer = bank. Ju = if. Karahi = you make. Nirmal = clean. Neer = water.
O Kabir! If you make your home (to live) on the bank of the Ganga, and keep drinking (the Ganga's) clean water,
Kabeer, some make their homes on the banks of the Ganges, and drink pure water.
Kabir, they who make their home on the bank of the Ganges and drink pure water,
Sri Kabir ji says: even if one makes one's home on the (teer) bank of the Ganga, and drinks the pure water of that same Ganga ji —
WN5S: Mukat = release (from vices, the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters'). Iu kah = saying this. Rame = remembers (Prabhu's Name). ||54||
even so, without devotion to Parmatma there can be no release (from vices, the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters'). Kabir, having said this, remembers Parmatma's Name alone. ||54||
Without devotional worship of the Lord, they are not liberated. Kabeer proclaims this. ||54||
even they are emancipated not without the Lord's meditation. Kabir proclaims this eternal truth.
yet without devotion to Hari there is never liberation. Saying this, (kabir) great souls, the saints, have absorbed themselves in devotion alone. ||54||
LK8B: O Kabir! (By living on the banks of the clean water of the Ganga and other pilgrimage places, lust and the rest do not let go, nor can the mind become pure; but) when (by remembering Parmatma's Name) my mind became pure like the clean water of the Ganga,
Kabeer, my mind has become immaculate, like the waters of the Ganges.
Kabir, my mind has become immaculate like the Ganges' water.
Sri Kabir ji says: my mind has become pure like the water of the Ganga ji.
A7VY: then Parmatma will go about following me, (calling) "Kabir, Kabir". ||55||
The Lord follows after me, calling, "Kabeer! Kabeer!" ||55||
The Lord follows me, saying "Kabir, O my Kabir".
Because of that, Hari Himself goes about following me, saying "Kabir, Kabir"; that is, He is my helper, ever with me. ||55||
TVNM: Hardee = turmeric. Peearee = yellow, of yellow colour. Oojal bhaai = of white colour, white.
O Kabir! Turmeric is yellow in colour, lime is white (but when the two meet, both lose their colour and a red colour arises; in the same way)
Kabeer, tumeric is yelow, and lime is white.
Kabir, yellow is the turmeric and white in colour is the lime.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as turmeric is yellow and lime is white in every (bhaai) way, and by the meeting of the two a colour arises —
D6VY: Sanehee = one who loves. Tau = then. Donau baran = both castes, high and low (the distinction between them). ||56||

know that the person who loves Parmatma has met Parmatma when that person wipes out (the distinction between) both castes, high and low (and within them arises the understanding to see the light of the One Prabhu in all beings). ||56||
You shall meet the Beloved Lord, only when both colors are lost. ||56||
Then alone is the Beloved Lord met, when both the colours are lost.
so too Ram and Ram's (sanehee) beloved (milai) become one with each other when both give up their own colour. ||56||
GZ17: Peeratan = yellowness, yellow colour. Harai = takes away. Choon chihan = the mark of lime, the white colour of lime. Na rahaai = does not remain.

O Kabir! (When turmeric and lime meet,) the turmeric gives up its yellow colour, the white colour of the lime does not remain (in the same way, through the blessing of remembrance, the low spirits of low caste vanish from within the low-caste person, and the pride of loftiness goes from the mind of the high-caste person).
Kabeer, tumeric has lost its yellow color, and no trace of lime's whiteness remains.
Kabir, turmeric loses its yellowness and not even a trace of whiteness of lime remains.

Sri Kabir ji says: when the yellowness of limited knowledge of the turmeric that is the being is (harai) removed, and in the lime that is the bright Lord no mark of the whiteness of all-knowingness remains — meaning, through the implied sense, being and Lord become one —
ZUU6: Balihaaree = a sacrifice, devoted. Jih = through the blessing of which love. ||57||
I am a sacrifice to this love for Prabhu, through which (the distinction of) high and low caste, varna and lineage is wiped out. ||57||
I am a sacrifice to this love, by which social class and status, color and ancestry are taken away. ||57||
I am a sacrifice to this love, by which caste tribe and lineage are effaced.
I am a sacrifice to this love, through which the pride of caste, varna and lineage goes away. ||57||
5XUF: Mukat duaara = the door through which one can pass and be released from the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters' and the 'five boys'. Sankura = narrow. Dasaen bhaai = a tenth part.
O Kabir! The door through which one passes and is released from the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters' and the 'five boys' is very narrow; know it to be even a tenth part of a mustard seed,
Kabeer, the door of liberation is very narrow, less than the width of a mustard seed.
Kabir, narrow is the door of salvation, its breadth is one tenth part of a mustard seed.
Question: Sri Kabir ji says, the door of liberation, spiritual knowledge, is exceedingly (sankura) narrow, like a tenth part of a mustard seed — that is, extremely subtle.
30BG: Maigal = (Sanskrit madakal) a maddened elephant; drunk like an elephant with the pride of bathing at pilgrimage places and of birth in a high caste. Kiu kai = how? In what way? (That is, not at all.) Nikso jaai = can pass through. ||58||
but the person whose mind has become like a maddened elephant with the pride of bathing at pilgrimage places and of taking birth in a high caste cannot pass through this door. ||58||
Your mind is larger than an elephant; how will it pass through? ||58||
Your mind has overgrown like an elephant. How can it pass through?
This being's mind has become as bulky as a (maigal) elephant with ego; so how can it pass out through it? ||58||
776N: Tuttha = pleased. Pasaau = grace, mercy, kindness.
O Kabir! If one meets such a Guru who, being pleased, shows mercy (to the person),
Kabeer, if I meet such a True Guru, who mercifully blesses me with the gift,
O Kabir, if I meet with such a Guru, who in his mercy blesses me with the gift,

Answer: Sri Kabir ji says, if the seeker meets such a True Guru as is described in the Shastras — meaning, one learned in scripture and established in Braham — and, pleased, gives the gift of teaching,
31K1: Mokla = wide open. Sahje = in sahaj, remaining in the steady state, remaining beyond the turmoil of the 'five boys' and the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters'. Aavau jaau = you may come and go about your work. ||59||

then the door through which release from these, lust and the rest, is possible becomes wide open; staying in the steady state (gained from the Guru's door), you may then go freely about your work. ||59||
then the door of liberation will open wide for me, and I will easily pass through. ||59||
then the door of salvation would open wide and I will easily pass through it.

then for them the gaining of the door of liberation, spiritual knowledge, becomes (mokla) easy; and through it they go (sahje) into their true form and come into worldly dealings, and are always in bliss. ||59||
TH0J: Mohi = (the original word is 'mohi'; here it is read 'muhi', one measure shorter, to keep the metre) with me. Chhaan = thatched hut. Chhaapree = shack. Gaau = village.
O Kabir! I have neither a thatched hut nor a shack; I have neither a house nor a village;
Kabeer, I have no hut or hovel, no house or village.
Kabir! I have no shed nor any hut. I have neither a house nor a village.
Sri Kabir ji says: I have neither a big thatched hut nor a small shack, no house, and no village of my own.
PTXM: Mat = perhaps. Mere = with me (as a support). Naau = name, the prestige of ownership. ||60||

just as there is no distinction of caste in my mind, so there is no wish for the prestige of ownership. (If we give up pride of caste and possessiveness over Maya,) perhaps Parmatma will ask after (us). ||60||
I hope that the Lord will not ask who I am. I have no social status or name. ||60||
I have no caste and name and the Lord shall ask not who I am.
Lest Hari ask me, "Who are you?" — in me there is no caste, and I have no name. Meaning, giving up pride in all things, I have known the One Hari as the form of all. ||60||
EMRK: Muhi = to me. Marne ka = of ending the self, of dying to pride in good deeds, high caste and ownership. Chaau = longing. Marau = if I want to die this death. Ta = then.
O Kabir! Within me is a longing to end my self-centredness, to finish possessiveness; but this self-centredness can end only if we fall at Prabhu's door,
Kabeer, I long to die; let me die at the Lord's Door.
Kabir, I long to die, however, when I die, then, let it be at the Lord's door.
Sri Kabir ji says: I have an (chaau) eagerness to die; but when I die, let me die only at Hari's door, which is the true company.
6Y62: (so that it would be no wonder if, in His grace, that gracious) Prabhu should one day ask, "Who is this who has fallen at My door?" ||61||
I hope that the Lord does not ask, "Who is this, lying at my door?" ||61||
May the Lord not ask, "who is this man lying at my door?"

For perhaps sometime Hari will ask, "Who are you, lying at Our door?" Meaning, by going to the true company one will meet Hari. ||61|| ☬ Once, out of hostility, some Brahmins, to bring disgrace on Sri Kabir ji, sent letters to distant lands in Kabir ji's name announcing a feast, and summoned many robed holy men. All those robed men kept coming to Kabir ji's house. Seeing so many of them gathered, Kabir ji went and sat in a lonely place in a forest. Then Bhagvant took the form of a merchant and prepared the supplies for the feast, and, taking the form of Kabir ji, pleased all the saints and Brahmins and served many delicacies. Then Kabir ji's fame grew great; hearing of it he too came back from the forest, and Hari vanished. Then people said to Kabir ji, "Blessed is Kabir ji! Blessed is Kabir ji!" Hearing his own praise, Sri Kabir ji says for their sake:
D1BB: Naah ham keea = I did not do this; I did not have the strength to escape the blows of the "hundreds of thousands of hunters", lust and the rest, and join Prabhu's feet. Na karahige = nor in future can the strength come into me to face these vices myself. Na kar sakai sareer = this body of mine too is not able of itself to find such strength, for its senses keep driving it towards vices.

O Kabir! It was not my own strength that I could escape the blows of the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters', lust and the rest, and join Prabhu's feet; nor in future can the strength come into me to face these vices myself; this body of mine is simply not able enough.
Kabeer, I have not done anything; I shall not do anything; my body cannot do anything.
Kabir, I have done is not, nor will I do it, nor can my body do it.
O brother! We did not put on this show of a feast, nor will we do such a thing in future, because our body can do nothing.
P53Z: Kia jaanau = who knows? It is no wonder that; the real truth must be that. Kichh = whatever has been done, whatever devotion has been done by overcoming lust and the rest. Kabir = great. ||62||
The truth is that whatever little devotion I have managed by overcoming lust and the rest, Prabhu Himself has done it all, and (by His grace) Kabir (the devotee) has become famous. ||62||
I do not know what the Lord has done, but the call has gone out: "Kabeer, Kabeer." ||62||
What do I know as to what my God has done, that Kabir is acclaimed all over.
What do I know? That is, I know nothing. O brother! Hari Himself has done all this, through which Kabir has become (known) in the world. ||62|| ☬ He makes known the glory of the Name:
3T8T: Supnai hoo = even in a dream. Barrarraai kai = talking in one's sleep; when dreaming one sometimes begins to speak, and this is called talking in one's sleep. Jih mukh = from whose mouth. Niksai = comes out.
O Kabir! If, talking aloud in a dream while asleep, Parmatma's Name comes out of some person's mouth,
Kabeer, if someone utters the Name of the Lord even in dreams,
Kabir, from whose mouth, even in dream, issues the Lord's Name as he mutters;
Sri Kabir ji says: the one from whose mouth Ram's Name is uttered even when talking in a dream —
DT7C: Pag = feet. Paanhee = (Sanskrit upaanah) shoes. Chaam = skin, hide. ||63||
the skin of my body is ready for the shoes of their feet (that is, I am ready to serve them in every way). ||63||
I would make my skin into shoes for his feet. ||63||
Let the skin of my body be the shoes for his feet.
may the skin of my body become the (paanhee) shoes of their feet. Meaning, if uttering it in a dream earns such rank, then the glory of those who utter it openly with love is boundless. ||63||
PTGX: Pootre = puppets, figures. Raakhio = (the letter 'u' carries two vowel signs, (o) and (u); the original word is 'raakhio', here read 'raakhiu' to keep the metre).

O Kabir! We are figures of clay; we have given ourselves the name 'human' (but we remain figures of clay, because, forgetting the Parmatma who adorned this figure of ours and put His light into it, we are loving clay alone);
Kabeer, we are puppets of clay, but we take the name of mankind.
Kabir, we are the puppets of clay and bear the name of men.
Sri Kabir ji says: we are figures made of clay, and our name has been put down as 'human'. Meaning, the qualities of a human are not there; only the name has been kept.
LCCT: Paahune = guests. Roondhahi = we occupy. Thaau = place. Bad bad = more and more. Maanas = human. ||64||
we are guests here for four days, but we keep occupying more and more space. ||64||
We are guests here for only a few days, but we take up so much space. ||64||
Though, guests here for only four days, we occupy very great space.
We are guests of four days — meaning, life is brief — and we are (roondhahi) taking over great places; meaning, we make great schemes. ||64||
Q0XN: Mahidee kar = like henna. Ghaalia = laboured, toiled. Aap = oneself. Peesaai peesaai = grinding and grinding, subjecting (oneself) to the hardships of austerities and the like.
O Kabir! (Henna is ground and ground fine and then applied to the feet. In this way the hardships the henna bears are, as it were, accepted; but)
Kabeer, I have made myself into henna, and I grind myself into powder.
Kabir I have made myself into henna and have thoroughly ground myself.
Sri Kabir ji says: this soul-bride ground her body like henna — meaning, gave it great hardship through chanting, austerity and the like.
36KX: Sah = O Husband! Tai baat na poochheeai = You did not even ask after them, You paid no attention, You did not even turn to look. Kabahu = ever. Na laaee paai = did not apply to the feet, did not join to the feet (as someone applies ground henna to the feet). ||65||

the person who laboured hard, subjecting themselves to the hardships of austerities and the like, as henna is ground and ground fine — O Prabhu! You did not even turn to look at their toil; You never joined them to Your feet. ||65||
But You, O my Husband Lord, have not asked about me; You have never applied me to Your Feet. ||65||
However, you, O Groom, has inquired not about me and has not applied me to Yours feet ever.

But without the Guru's teaching that (sah) Master Hari never even asked after her, nor ever joined her to His feet. Meaning, that Master neither made her one with Himself nor was pleased with her. ||65||
ED8B: Hatkai = stops, checks, holds back from the right path of life. Aavat jaatiahu = one who comes and goes, one who always comes and goes, one who always stays, one who stays for ever. Koe = any of the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters' or the 'five boys'.
O Kabir! The door at which, staying (always), no one (of the 'hundreds of thousands of hunters', the 'five boys' and the rest) can block (the right path of life) —
Kabeer, that door, through which people never stop coming and going
Kabir, the door at which no one is stopped from coming and going,
Sri Kabir ji says: the door of the true company, at which no one (hatkai) stops those who come and go —
YWL5: Kaise chhoddeeai = should not be left. Aisa = such. Dar = door, Prabhu's feet, Prabhu's support. ||66||
a door that is such should never be left. ||66||
- how can I leave such a door as that? ||66||
how can that kind of door be left, which is such a type?
so how can one leave a door that is so unbarred? Meaning, it is fitting to keep its company always. ||66||
8YA9: Jarjara = very old. Dooba tha = I was sinking. Pai = but. Ubrio = came out, was saved from sinking. Jhabak = with a surge. Lahar jhabak = with the surge of the waves, with the push of the waves. Gun = Prabhu's praise. Gun jhabak = with the surge of the wave of Prabhu's praise.
O Kabir! I was sinking (in the world-ocean), but with the push of the wave of Prabhu's praise I was lifted up (out of the surges of worldly attachment).
Kabeer, I was drowning, but the waves of virtue saved me in an instant.
Kabir I was drowning, however, the wave of virtues quickly saved me.

Sri Kabir ji says: in the ocean of the world are the pleasures of the senses, with the waves of the qualities. I had sunk in them, but then through the Guru's teaching I came up out of it (jhabak) quickly and was saved.

2TCN: Hau = I. Pharak = with a leap, leaping, at once. ||67||

(Before, I was drunk on attachment; now my eyes opened;) at that moment I saw (that the ship of bodily attachment on which I was riding) was quite old (riddled with holes by vices). I leapt down (from that ship of "mine") (I gave up the sense of "mine", attachment to the body. But all this was because I did not leave that 'door' at which, staying, 'no one can block'). ||67||
When I saw that my boat was rotten, then I immediately got out. ||67||
When I saw the ship was rotten, the, I got down all at once.
For when I saw that the ship of the body was (jarjara) bound to perish, then I got down from it and (pharak) stood apart; meaning, I came to know my own true form as distinct from the body. ||67||
CWE6: Na bhaavaee = does not seem good. Na suhaai = does not please.

O Kabir! (Although there is this blessing in staying at Prabhu's door, in singing Prabhu's praise, that one is saved from sinking in the world-ocean, yet) the person full of vices does not like devotion to Parmatma; worship of Parmatma does not please them (does not seem to give comfort).
Kabeer, the sinner does not like devotion to the Lord; he does not appreciate worship.
Kabir, a sinner loves not Lord's meditation yea, the God's worship does not please him,
Sri Kabir ji says: the sinful person does not like Hari's devotion, which is chanting the Name, nor does Hari's worship please them.
UEMF: Parharai = gives up. Jah = where. Bigandh = stench. ||68||
(The nature of a person full of vices becomes like a fly's:) a fly leaves (fragrant) sandalwood and goes where there is a stench. ||68||
The fly abandons the sandalwood tree, and goes after the rotten smell. ||68||
like the fly that forsakes sandal and goes there where there is an evil odour.
Just as a fly leaves sandalwood and goes where there is a stench, so sinful people run from the true company and go to bad company. ||68||
8SSZ: Baid = one who treats the sick; one who tries to save people full of vices from spiritual death by teaching them. Mooa = died (weeping), died (weeping for the pleasures of Maya), died (the spiritual death of wearing oneself out for the pleasures of Maya).

O Kabir! (Wearing itself out for the pleasures of Maya,) the whole world is dying (the spiritual death of sinking in the world-ocean, in attachment to Maya), whether one is sick or one is a physician (that is, on one side are those who, being ignorant and foolish, do not know the path of life at all and are caught in vices; on the other are the learned pandits who teach the foolish. But the state of both is that all their running about is only for the pleasures of Maya; their senses are wearing themselves out each for its own sense-pleasures, weeping for pleasures. Being without devotion to the One, they are all dead with spiritual death).
Kabeer, the physician is dead, and the patient is dead; the whole world is dead.
Kabir, the physician is dead, the patient is dead and dead is the whole world.
Sri Kabir ji says: the physician too died, and the sick one too died, and the whole world too has died — that is, perished.
4WN6: Ek = only that person. Jih = whose. Rovanhaar = one who weeps, who wears themselves out weeping, who wears themselves out for the pleasures of Maya. Naahee = none. ||69||

O Kabir! Only that person does not die (spiritual death) none of whose (companions, the senses) is weeping (for the pleasures of Maya) (wearing itself out; and such a person can only be the one who does not leave Prabhu's door, for staying at Prabhu's door 'no one can block'). ||69||
