Only Kabeer is not dead; there is no one to mourn for him. ||69||
Kabir alone is not dead for whom there is no one to weep.

Only the company of great-souled saints has not died, because in their mind there is not the ignorance that makes all beings weep. Or: only Parmeshvar does not die, who has no one to weep for Him; meaning, He is free of dying and of relatives. ||69||
W7LB: Khor = hollow, hollowness. Motee khor laagee = a big hollow keeps forming within them; vices keep hollowing them out from within, and they slowly die a spiritual death.
O Kabir! Every person who has not remembered Parmatma is hollowed out from within by vices (and slowly dies a spiritual death).
Kabeer, I have not meditated on the Lord; such is the bad habit I have developed.
Kabir, the mortal meditates not on the Lord. Such a great evil habit has attached to him.

Sri Kabir ji says: this being has not meditated on Ram's Name, because the (khor) leftovers of the senses — or the husks — have seemed (motee) dear. The juiceless peelings of sugarcane are called khoree. Or: the (khor) burrow of the body has seemed dear to it.
85LY: Kaaia = body. Na charhai = does not go up (on the stove). Bahor = again, a second time. ||70||
Just as a pot of wood, (once burnt on the stove,) cannot go on (the stove) again, so is this body (of the person burnt to death in the fire of vices; it does not get it a second time). ||70||
The body is a wooden pot; it cannot be put back on the fire. ||70||
The body is a wooden pot. It cannot be put on the fire again.
O brother! The wooden pot of the body does not go on the fire again. Meaning, having gained this human birth, secure your own good; otherwise, once it perishes, gaining it again is hard. ||70||
C1V8: Hoe paree = has come about. Aisee hoe paree = such a thing has come about, a wondrous joy has arisen. Keen = has made, Prabhu has made. Man ko bhaavat = the thing that has pleased the mind.
The person to whom Prabhu gives the gift (of devotion) that pleases the mind, on whom this wondrous mercy falls, that person too gives up self-centredness joyfully.
Kabeer, it came to pass, that I did whatever I pleased.
Kabir, it has so happened that I did what pleased my mind.
Sri Kabir ji says: when, through the Guru, I did the work the mind longed for — understanding the purport of the Shastras — then such a way came about; meaning, fearlessness came.
R0XZ: Marne = death, death to self-centredness. Te = from. Kia darapna = why be afraid? One should not be afraid. Haath = in the hand. Sidhaura = the coconut to which vermilion has been applied. ||71||
O Kabir! When a woman (on her husband's death) takes a vermilion-smeared coconut in her hand, she is not afraid of dying. ||71||
Why should I be afraid of death? I have invited death for myself. ||71||
Why should I now fear death when I have taken red lead in my hand?

For when the sati took the (sidhaura) coconut in her hand and the warrior took the sword, so too when the seeker took on detachment and the knower of reality took the sword of spiritual knowledge, then what fear of dying do they have? That is, they do not fear. ||71||
828V: Ras ko gaando = the cane of juice, a cane full of juice. Chooseeai = is sucked, is crushed, bears the hardship of being crushed (in return for giving juice it has to pay this price, that it is crushed in the press). Gun kau = for the sake of virtues, in exchange for virtues. Mareeai = one has to die, one has to give up self-centredness. Roe = weeping, giving up (faults).

O Kabir! The cane full of juice is crushed (in the press) (that is, in return for the gift of juice it has to pay this price, that it is crushed in the press); (so, in exchange for virtues, one has to give up faults and die to self-centredness).
Kabeer, the mortals suck at the sugar cane, for the sake of the sweet juice. They should work just as hard for virtue.
Kabir, just as man sucks sugarcane for the sake of sweet-juice, so should he strive hard for virtue.

Sri Kabir ji says: the saints are the (gaando) cane of juice; through their company, suck — that is, chant — Vahiguru's Name. And until qualities such as equanimity are gained, let us, seeing their virtues, weep before them. Meaning, giving up ego before them, let us speak words of humility, that virtues may be gained.
47QC: Maansai = to a person. Kahi hai = will say. ||72||

(The person who does not give up self-centredness and inclines only towards vices —) no one (in the world) calls that person of faults good (that is, they stay without the gift of devotion, and also earn disgrace in the world). ||72||
The person who lacks virtue - no one calls him good. ||72||
No one calls him good, who is without virtue
For no one calls a person of faults good; that is, everyone calls them bad. ||72||
2VMN: Gaagar = (clay) pot. Aaj kaalh = today or tomorrow, in a few days. Phoot jaihai = will break, will crack.

O Kabir! An unbaked clay pot may be full of water, but it breaks soon (such too is the lot of this body; it cannot last for ever. To gain the purpose of human birth, one must give up attachment to this body before it perishes, give up one's own will and walk the path shown by the Guru; but)
Kabeer, the pitcher is full of water; it will break, today or tomorrow.
Kabir the pitcher is full of water, It shall break today or tomorrow.
Sri Kabir ji says: this pot of the body, filled with the water of the breaths, will crack today or tomorrow — that is, will perish.
KA4Q: Ju = those people who. Na chetahi = do not keep in mind. Adh maajh = in the middle, halfway. Leejahige loot = will be robbed. ||73||

the people who do not keep their Guru in mind (who, caught in attachment to the body, forget the Guru and the path the Guru showed) are robbed halfway along the journey of life (lust and the other vices snare them and destroy all their virtues; in vices their capital here is spent and the next world is spoilt too). ||73||
Those who do not remember their Guru, shall be plundered on the way. ||73||
They, who contemplate not their Guru, they shall be plundered on the way.

The people who do not remember Hari's Name through their True Guru, or do not remember their True Guru, will be robbed halfway along the road. Meaning, when on dying Yama takes them, and on the way they grow thirsty, they are given a cup of water in exchange for the fruit of their merits; in this way their merits are robbed on the way itself. So those who chant the Name are always happy, because Yama's messengers do not come near them. ||73||
5QUB: Kookar = dog. Ko = of. Muteea = (beautiful) pearl.
O Kabir! I am the dog of (the door of) my Master-Prabhu (I stay always at Prabhu's door, and because of this) my name has become 'Pearl' (that is, the world too calls me with love).
Kabeer, I am the Lord's dog; Moti is my name.
Kabir, I am the Lord's dog and Moti, is my Name.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, I am Ram's dog, with a mind pure as a pearl — or 'Pearl' is really my name; meaning, I am dear to the Guru.
LHNK: Jah = where, wherever. Khinchai = pulls. Jaau = I go. ||74||
My Master-Prabhu has put a rope around my neck; wherever He pulls me, there I go. ||74||
There is a chain around my neck; wherever I am pulled, I go. ||74||
There is chain on my neck, and go I, where I am pulled with the chain.
Around our neck lies the rope of His command. So wherever He pulls, there I go; meaning, we walk in His command. ||74||
U3AT: Japnee = rosary. Kaath kee = of tulsi, rudraksh and the like. Loe = to the people in the world.
O Kabir! Why do you go about showing people the rosary of tulsi, rudraksh and the like (in your hand)?
Kabeer, why do you show other people your rosary beads?
Kabir, why you display your wooden rosary to people?
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, taking a wooden (japnee) rosary in your hands, what are you showing people?
SFED: Na chethee = na chetahi, you do not remember. Kia hoe = no gain. ||75||
You do not remember Parmatma in your heart; this rosary (held in the hand) can be of no gain. ||75||
You do not remember the Lord in your heart, so what use is this rosary to you? ||75||
In your mind you remember not the Lord; of what avail is this rosary to you?
For when you do not remember Ram in your heart, what will come of turning this rosary? Meaning, nothing will be achieved by it. ||75||
3M0Y: Birah = separation, the feeling of being separated from Parmatma, the pang that "I am separated from Parmatma". Bhuyangam = snake. Man = in the mind. Na maanai = does not accept, cannot be charmed.

O Kabir! (The 'wooden rosary' can mend nothing, but) the person in whose mind, through the Guru's shelter, the snake of separation comes to dwell (the person who gains from the Guru's door the understanding that these, lust and the rest, have separated me from God) — no mantra (of lust and the rest) can work on them.
Kabeer, the snake of separation from the Lord abides within my mind; it does not respond to any mantra.
Kabir, the serpent of separation from the Lord abides within my mind and it yields to no charm.
Sri Kabir ji says: the one in whose mind dwells the snake of (birah) love, or separation, heeds no one's mantra of worldly engagement.
VZ4D: Ram biogee = the person who feels separation from Parmatma, who feels the pang that "through the pleasures of Maya I am cut off from God", who has been bitten by the snake of separation. Na jeeai = cannot live (for vices), cannot live (in self-centredness). Baura = mad. ||76||

The person who feels separation from Parmatma cannot live at all (that is, the feeling of separation from Parmatma is such a bite that one bitten by it cannot live for the pleasures of Maya); the life they do live is, in the world's eyes, the life of a madman. ||76||
One who is separated from the Lord does not live; if he does live, he goes insane. ||76||
He, who is separated from his Lord, lives not it he lives, then, becomes he insane.

For one separated from Ram, first of all, does not live at all; meaning, gives the mind no share in the dealings of the world. And if by chance, through past karma, they do live — that is, give it a share — they give it like one gone mad, because their mind always stays devoted to Braham. ||76||
2F6C: Chandnai = in sandalwood. Paaras chandnai = paarsai chandnai, in the philosopher's stone and in sandalwood. Tin hai = in these, the stone and the sandalwood. Sugandh = quality, fragrance.
O Kabir! The philosopher's stone and sandalwood — in both of these there is one quality;
Kabeer, the philosopher's stone and sandalwood oil have the same good quality.
Kabir, the philosopher's stone and sandal, they have the same good quality.
Sri Kabir ji says: the philosopher's stone and sandalwood — the two have one and the same (sugandh) nature.
NLBH: Tih mil = meeting these, the stone and the sandalwood. Teoo = they too, that wood and iron too. Kaath nirgandh = wood with no fragrance. ||77||

iron and fragrance-less wood, touching these, become excellent (iron touching the stone becomes gold; an ordinary tree, living near sandalwood, becomes fragrant. In the same way a person once sold to lust and the rest, meeting the Guru, becomes one who feels 'separation from Ram'). ||77||
Whatever comes into contact with them is uplifted. Iron is transformed into gold, and ordinary wood becomes fragrant. ||77||
Whatever comes into their contact, that becomes sublime Iron it transmuted into gold and the odorouless wood is rendered fragrant?

For by meeting those two they have become excellent: iron becomes gold, and wood that was without fragrance becomes fragrant. So too, by keeping the company of the saints, even dull beings attain excellence. ||77||
S0TU: Thenga = blow, stroke. Oh = that blow.
O Kabir! (Staying under the sway of lust and the rest, Yama's rod strikes the head, and one falls into the round of birth and death; and) this blow of Yama is so bad that it is very hard to bear.
Kabeer, Death's club is terrible; it cannot be endured.
Kabir, bad is the death's club, that is hard to endure.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, Yama's (thenga) club is bad — that is, painful. In the end the being will not be able to bear it.
91QA: Saadhoo = the Guru. Mohi = (the original word is 'mohi'; here it is read 'muhi'; the letter 'm' carries both vowel signs (o) and (u)) to me. Tinh = he. Anchal = with the hem, with the skirt of the robe. ||78||
(By Parmatma's grace) I met the Guru; he attached me to the hem of his robe (and I did not fall into the hands of lust and the rest). ||78||
I have met with the holy man; he has attached me to the hem of his robe. ||78||
I have met with a saint and he has attached me to his skirt.
The one holy man, Ramanand ji, who met me has attached me to the (anchal) hem of his grace; meaning, the True Guru alone is the one who saves from it. ||78||
DEDM: Baid = physician. Hau hee = I alone. Bhala = wise. Merai vas = in my control.
O Kabir! The physician says he is very wise; the cure is in his control (to save the soul from separating from the body when disease comes) (he knows how to treat disease).
Kabeer, the physician says that he alone is good, and all the medicine is under his control.
Kabir the physician says, I alone am good. All medicines are in my power.
Sri Kabir ji says: the physician says, "I alone am good; how capable I am, because giving medicine is in my control."
K7HZ: Ih = this soul. Basat = thing. Khas lei = snatches away. ||79||

But this soul is a thing (given in trust) by the Master-Prabhu; when He wishes, He takes it back (from the body) (one is not to stay here for ever; so keep in mind the blow of Yama, and coming to the Guru's door, 'die weeping for virtues'). ||79||
But these things belong to the Lord; He takes them away whenever He wishes. ||79||
However, this thing belongs to Lord, He takes it away, when He wills.
But, O brother, this thing, the power of life, has been given by Gopal; when it pleases Him, He will snatch it away. So nothing is in anyone's control.
ZFCD: Naubat = drum. Aapnee naubat bajaai lehu = enjoy yourself as you please.
O Kabir! (If you will not listen to this, then as you wish,) enjoy yourself as you please (but these pleasures are only) for ten days.
Kabeer, take your drum and beat it for ten days.
Kabir! Let any one beat one's drum for ten days.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, you too beat your drum of engagement in worldly deeds for some ten days.
BPML: Naav = boat. Sanjog = meeting, union. Nadee...jiu = like the meeting of travellers sitting in a boat to cross a river (they never all meet again). Bahur = again. Na mili hai = will not be met, (human birth) will not be gained. ||80||
Just as travellers sitting in a boat to cross a river meet (and never all meet again), so (this human body, wasted in self-willed pleasures) will not be gained again. ||80||
Life is like people meeting on a boat on a river; they shall not meet again. ||80||
This world is like the meeting of persons on a river-boat, who shall not meet again.

Like the meeting of those who board a boat on a river is this being's union with the body. When separation from it comes, after that this human body does not come to this being again. ||80|| ☬ He makes known the endlessness of Hari's praise:
ZR6Y: Mas = ink. Karau = I make. Banraai = all vegetation, all trees and plants.
O Kabir! If I make (the water of) all seven seas into ink, make pens from all the trees and plants, use the whole earth in place of paper,
Kabeer, if I could change the seven seas into ink and make all the vegetation my pen,
Kabir, if I make the seven oceans my ink, make the entire vegetation my pen,
Sri Kabir ji says: if one makes (mas) ink of the seven seas, and makes pens of the king of all forests — that is, of all wood —
174M: Basudha = earth. Kaagad = paper (Note: the letter 'z' is sometimes pronounced like 'd', as in kaazee or kaadee, hazoor or hadoor, haazar or haadar). Jau = if. Jas = glory, virtues. ||81||
even so Parmatma's virtues cannot be (fully) written down (that is, a person does not sing Parmatma's virtues in order to find their end and describe them all). ||81||
and the earth my paper, even then, I could not write the Praises of the Lord. ||81||
and make the earth my paper, even then, I can write not the God's praises.

and even if one makes the whole (basudha) earth into paper, still the praise of that Hari cannot be written; meaning, it is endless. ||81|| ☬ Someone said, "Why are you proud? Your caste is only that of a weaver." Or: once Bhagvant met him, and people said, "Keep away." To this he says:
XL1Y: Kia karai = can do no harm, cannot make me feel powerless.

O Kabir! (By singing Prabhu's virtues one cannot reach the end of His virtues, but through the blessing of His praise) my (low) weaver caste cannot make me feel powerless, because now the Parmatma, Master of creation, dwells in my heart.
Kabeer, what can my lowly status as a weaver do to me? The Lord dwells in my heart.
Kabir, what harm can my weaver's caste do to me, when the Lord abides in my mind?
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, what lack will the weaver caste bring? Meaning, it can bring no lack, because Gopal dwells in my heart.
XMQM: Ramaeea kanth mil = embrace Prabhu, join in the remembrance of Prabhu. Chookahi = will end. ||82||
O Kabir! Join in Prabhu's remembrance; (not only the weakness of low caste but) all the entanglements of Maya will end. ||82||
Kabeer, the Lord hugs me close in His Embrace; I have forsaken all my entanglements. ||82||
Kabir, the Pervading God, has taken me into His embrace and I am rid of all my involvement.
By meeting in the embrace of Ram, all-pervading and greatest of all — that is, by becoming one with Him — all (janjaal) bonds have gone. ||82||
F2RB: Ko nahee = only a rare one is. Mandar = body, attachment to the body, identification with the body. Jaraai dei = burns.
O Kabir! (Though there is great blessing in praise, yet attachment to the body and lust and the rest are so strong that) only a rare person burns their attachment to the body,
Kabeer, will anyone set fire to his home
Kabir, their is not any such person, who may set fire to his place.
Sri Kabir ji says: there is no one — that is, it is rare — who burns up the pride of the temple of the body,
BYJF: Paanchau larike = the five sons of Maya, lust and the rest. Liu = attention, love. ||83||
only a rare one who, killing the five sons of Maya, lust and the rest, keeps their attention fixed on Prabhu. ||83||
and kill his five sons (the five thieves) to remain lovingly attached to the Lord? ||83||
Slaying his five sons, he remains attached to the love of his Lord.
and, killing the five sons of the mind, lust and the rest, fixing the mind on the One Name of Ram alone, stays steady. ||83||
UFUP: Tan = body, attachment to the body. Phook devai = burns. Andha = blinded, blind with attachment to the body, so drunk on identification with the body that the right path of life is not seen.
O Kabir! (Because of the influence of Maya) only a rare one is found who (sings Prabhu's praise and) burns attachment to the body.
Kabeer, will anyone burn his own body?
Kabir, there is no such man, who may burn this body of his.
Sri Kabir ji says: there is no one who (phook) burns up the pride of this body.
TGJQ: Kook rahio = is calling out loudly. ||84||
The world is so sunk in attachment that it cannot see its own good, (even though) Kabir is calling it out loudly. ||84||
The people are blind - they do not know, although Kabeer continues to shout at them. ||84||
The blind man realises not his Lord, though Kabir continues to shout at him.
But this crowd of people, blind through ignorance, does not understand. (Kabira) Kabir ji says: I am calling out loudly. ||84||
2286: Satee = the woman who mounts the pyre with her dead husband. Chih = pyre. He beer masaan = O brother cremation ground! O beloved fire of the cremation grounds!
O Kabir! The woman who is ready to burn herself with the body of her husband who has reached the next world, to meet him, mounts the pyre and says boldly: "O brother cremation ground!
Kabeer, the widow mounts the funeral pyre and cries out, "Listen, O brother funeral pyre.
Kabir, mounted on the pyre, the widow cries out, "Hear, O my brethren who have come this cremation ground,
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, the sati, mounted on the (chih) pyre — or (chih) out of breath — calls out like this: "Listen, O (beer) brother! You have come to this cremation ground, so I say to you:
3NQY: Sabaaia = all. Chal gaio = has gone away, has left one's side. Nidaan = in the end, at last. Kaam = need, dealing, purpose. Ham tum kaam = I have need of you. Pukaarai = says loudly, says boldly. ||85||
Listen: all my relatives have left my side (no one could unite me with my husband); in the end, O brother, it is you I have need of." ||85||
All people must depart in the end; it is only you and I." ||85||
all the persons have departed, ultimately, the thing of use to me and to you is the Lord's meditation".

Your fathers, grandfathers and the whole crowd of people have gone on ahead through this very place, and now we too are going, and in the end your business too will be here." Or: the truthful people on whom the (chih) passion of spiritual knowledge and detachment has come call out like this: "O brother, why have you died away from Parmeshvar? The crowd of people doing 'I' and 'mine' has gone. So to hold on to 'I' and 'mine' is the work of (nidaan) ignorant fools; so give up 'I' and 'mine'." ||85||

CX3F: Dah dis = in all ten directions, on every side, towards countless things of Maya. Ud ud = flying again and again, wandering again and again.

(O Kabir! Even knowing that Prabhu's praise burns vices and joins one to Prabhu's feet,) a person's mind becomes a bird (and, leaving the support of the One Prabhu,) wandering and wandering (after the things of Maya), runs in all ten directions.
Kabeer, the mind has become a bird; it soars and flies in the ten directions.
Kabir, the mind has become like a bird, flying and taking wing, it goes in ten directions.
Sri Kabir ji says: the mind has become like a bird. Flying and flying it goes in all ten directions; meaning, it keeps making countless schemes.
WDH4: (And it is the very law of nature that) whatever company a person sits in, such fruit they receive. ||86||
According to the company it keeps, so are the fruits it eats. ||86||
As is the company it associates with, so is the fruit it eats.
Because of that, whatever kind of company a person joins, such fruit they eat — that is, enjoy. ||86||
DQGX: O Kabir! (By singing Prabhu's praise, singing Prabhu's virtues, one cannot reach the end of the virtues; but with the help of praise) the place I was searching for (the place of Prabhu's feet) — that very place I have found.
Kabeer, you have found that place which you were seeking.
Kabir, you have obtained the place, which you were searching.
Sri Kabir ji says: the Vahiguru we were searching for, we have found in the place of the inner mind itself. How was He found?
D4KT: Phir kai = turning, being changed. Ja kau = which (place). ||87||

O Kabir! The One (Prabhu) whom you used to call 'someone else' (whom you used to think separate from yourself) — you (through the blessing of praise) have been changed into His very form (merged in Him, become one with Him). ||87||
You have become that which you thought was separate from yourself. ||87||
You yourself have turned to be the One, whom you thought to be different from you.
O mind! The One you used to call another form, or someone else — meaning, whom you knew as hidden — when you (phir kai) turned inward and looked, then you yourself became that form. ||87||
LBY5: Marau = I will die, my soul will die a spiritual death. Kusang kee maaree = struck by bad company, by sitting in bad company, coming under the influence of vices. Nikat = near. Ju = as, just as. Ber = jujube tree.

O Kabir! (If you give up Parmatma's praise, you will naturally keep company with those who are cut off from Prabhu; but see,) never keep company with people cut off from God. If a jujube tree grows near a banana plant —
Kabeer, I have been ruined and destroyed by bad company, like the banana plant near the thorn bush.
Kabir, I am destroyed and ruined by the evil company, like the plantain near the wild caper.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as the jujube near the banana is bad company for that banana, and struck by it that row of bananas dies —
PFFQ: Uh jhoolai = the jujube sways with the wind. Uh cheereeai = that banana is torn. Na her = do not look at. Saakat = a person cut off from God, one who has forgotten Parmatma's remembrance. ||88||
the jujube sways with the wind, and the banana is torn (by its thorns); so (O Kabir!) sitting in bad company, under the influence of vices, your soul will die a spiritual death. ||88||
The thorn bush waves in the wind, and pierces the banana plant; see this, and do not associate with the faithless cynics. ||88||
The latter waves and the former is pierced through by its thorns, So see you not even, the sinner's society.

the banana sways as if fanning it, or offering itself to the jujube, and the jujube in return tears it with thorns. In the same way, the saakat does harm to the Gurmukh who does good. So, O brother, do not even look at the company of the saakat. ||88||
DW53: Bhaar paraaee = the burden of others' (slander). Sir charai = climbs onto the person's head, climbs onto the head of the one caught in 'bad company'. Baat = path. Chalio chaahai baat = (the burden keeps climbing, yet the person) likes to walk that very path (of slander).
O Kabir! (Because of bad company) the burden of (slandering) others keeps climbing onto this person's head (the burden keeps climbing, yet the person) likes to walk that very path (of slander);
Kabeer, the mortal wants to walk on the path, carrying the load of others' sins on his head.
Kabir, man wishes to tread the path, carrying on his head the load of others sins.

Sri Kabir ji says: the burden of others — of worship and honour and of providing for relatives — is climbing onto this being's head, and today or tomorrow they want to set out on the road to the next world.
BXXM: Apne bhaarahi = of the burden of one's own (other vices committed). Aagai = before the person. Aughat ghaat = hard road. ||89||
before the person lies a very hard road, yet the burden (of their own other evil deeds) never even comes to mind. ||89||
He is not afraid of his own load of sins; the road ahead shall be difficult and treacherous. ||89||
He fears not the load of his own sins. The road ahead is difficult to tread.
They do not fear the burden of their own evil deeds. Because of this, further on, on the road to the next world, sinners will have to walk through (au ghat) hard (ghaat) places. ||89||
CKR1: Ban = forest. Daadhee laakree = burnt wood, wood turned to charcoal. Thaadhee = standing (that is, clearly, plainly).
O Kabir! (If you listen and understand with attention,) even charred wood from the forest (is heard) clearly calling out,
Kabeer, the forest is burning; the tree standing in it is crying out,
Kabir, the standing forest tree, which is burning, cries, out.
Sri Kabir ji says: just as forest wood burnt by fire, (thaadhee) standing, calls out —
NQ6B: Mat = lest. Bas = in the power, in the company. Luhaar = the person who spends all their life buying the coals of vices; the saakat, the person full of vices. ||90||
"Lest I fall into the hands of the blacksmith; he will burn me a second time." ||90||
"Do not let me fall into the hands of the blacksmith, who would burn me a second time." ||90||
Let me not fall into the hand of blacksmith, who would burn me a second time.

"Let me not fall into the blacksmith's power, for if I come under him, he will burn me a second time" — that is, as charcoal, again. In the same way the person of detachment calls out to the saints: "Having been burnt by detachment, let me not fall again into the power of the blacksmith Yama. For once the body will surely burn, but let Yama not burn the being a second time in the fire of hell." ||90||
UYKK: O Kabir! (By singing Prabhu's virtues one cannot reach the end of His virtues, but through the blessing of this praise the 'mind' dies; the 'mind' turns away from vices.) With the death of this one mind, one more also died — pride of caste; and in all two died — the mind and pride of caste. Then two more died — identification with the body and craving; in all it became four.
Kabeer, when one died, two were dead. When two died, four were dead.
Kabir, on the death of one, two died and on the death of two, four.
Sri Kabir ji says: by killing the one ego, both of these, attachment and aversion, died; by the death of these two, all four of these — lust, anger, greed and attachment — died.
21PG: Two more died — bad company and slander; and all these became six, four masculine ('men') and two feminine ('women'). ||91||
When four died, six were dead, four males and two females. ||91||
On the death of four, died six, four males and two females.

By the death of these four, these four men — birth, death, joy and grief — and two women, hunger and thirst — these six died. Or: by the death of the one, attachment to sense-objects, the second, aversion, also died. By the death of these two, the two, comfort and pain, died; with these four, two women, hope and craving — thus six died, that is, went away. ||91||
XZE3: Dekh dekh dhoondhia = searched, looking again and again. Kahoon na = nowhere. Thaur = place, a place for the mind to rest, a place where the mind finds peace, where the mind stops wandering.
O Kabir! I have searched the whole world with great effort; nowhere have I found such a place (where the mind stops wandering).
Kabeer, I have seen and observed, and searched all over the world, but I have found no place of rest anywhere.
Kabir, I have seen, looked around and searched the world, but I have found no place of rest anywhere.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, looking and looking into the Shastras and Vedas — that is, reading them again and again — I have searched the world. In it we have found no place of peace.
WWJD: Jin = the (person) who. Kaha aur = where else? Why somewhere else? Bhulaane = wander astray. ||92||

The person who has not remembered Parmatma's Name (has found no place of peace for the mind anywhere; Prabhu's Name alone, found in the true company, saves from wandering). (Giving up His praise,) why do you wander astray in other places? ||92||
Those who do not remember the Lord's Name - why do they delude themselves in other pursuits? ||92||
They, who remember not their God's Name, why do they wander in other pursuits?
So those who have not remembered Hari's Name — have they gone astray among other things? Meaning, all their works are useless. ||92||
K3V1: Ant = to the end, always. Karai nirbaahu = gives company, stays a companion.
O Kabir! (There is only one 'place' for the mind's peace; that is the 'holy company'; so) one should join the holy company; the company of the holy lasts to the end;
Kabeer, associate with the Holy people, who will take you to Nirvaanaa in the end.
Kabir, associate you only with the saint, who shall emancipate you in the end.
Sri Kabir ji says: keep the company of the saints alone, for it is what stands by one to the very end.
0EYA: Saakat sang = the company of one cut off from God. Ja te = from which (company). Binaahu = destruction, spiritual death. ||93||
one should not keep the company of people cut off from God; from it comes (the danger of) spiritual death. ||93||
Do not associate with the faithless cynics; they would bring you to ruin. ||93||
Associate you not with the mammon worshipper, through which, you shall be ruined.
Do not keep the company of saakats, by which in the end there is only (binaahu) ruin. ||93||
U5J9: Jag mah = jag mah (aai), coming into the world, taking birth in the world. Jaan kai = recognising.

O Kabir! (The place of peace for the mind is Prabhu's Name alone; so) those who, taking birth in the world, have remembered that Prabhu, recognising that He pervades the whole world (count them alone as born into the world; their birth alone is fruitful; they are the holy, and their company is the holy company).
Kabeer, I contemplate the Lord in the world; I know that He is permeating the world.
Kabir, realising that the Lord is contained in the world, contemplate His I in this world.
Sri Kabir ji says: those who have remembered Vahiguru in the world, knowing Him to be all-pervading — their praise has spread through the whole world.
H3SX: Baadahi = in vain. Aai janme = came and were born. ||94||
Those who have not remembered Parmatma's Name were born in vain. ||94||
Those who do not contemplate the Name of the Lord - their birth into this world is useless. ||94||
They, who meditate not on the God's Name, have been born in vain in this world.
Those who have not remembered Hari's Name have come into the world and been born in vain. ||94||
VLPY: Aasa...kee = hope in Parmatma, look to Parmatma for support. Niraas = nir-aas, without hope.
O Kabir! (If you want a 'place' of peace for the mind, then, joining the 'holy company') one should rest one's hope on the One Parmatma and give up other hopes.
Kabeer, place your hopes in the Lord; other hopes lead to despair.
Kabir lean you on the Lord's hope alone. All other hopes lead to despair.
Sri Kabir ji says: hope in the One Ram alone, and stay free of other hopes.
V8Q0: Narak parahi = fall into hell, stay always in pain. Maanaee = people. ||95||
The people who turn their face from Parmatma's remembrance stay fallen in hell (stay always in pain). ||95||
Those who dissociate themselves from the Lord's Name - when they fall into hell, then they will appreciate its value. ||95||
They, who forsake the God's Name, shall realise its worth, when they fall into hell.
Those who stay indifferent to chanting Hari's Name — that is, who do not chant Hari's Name — those (maanaee) people go and fall into hells. ||95||
XX8V: Sikh = disciples, hangers-on. Keso = (Sanskrit Keshav — the One with long hair, Hari) Parmatma.
O Kabir! Those who did not make Parmatma their friend (did not form a bond with Parmatma, and) made many disciples and hangers-on —
Kabeer has made many students and disciples, but he has not made God his friend.
Kabir has made many disciples and followers, however, he has not made God his friend.
Sri Kabir ji says: they made countless (sikh saakha) disciples and disciples' disciples, but did not make Vahiguru their friend.
88AK: Chaale the = had set out, had made the effort. Attakio = got stuck. ||96||

(though at first) they made the effort to meet Parmatma, their mind got stuck on the way (they became busy having their disciples serve and worship them, forgot Prabhu's remembrance, and the 'place' of peace for the mind was not their lot). ||96||
He set out on a journey to meet the Lord, but his consciousness failed him half-way. ||96||
He had set out to meet his God, however, his mind failed him halfway.

Those people had set out to meet Hari, but on the way their mind got stuck. Meaning, they took on the garb of faqirs to worship Hari, and, trapped in worldly engagement, they have become empty of remembrance. ||96||
L7FK: Kaaran = means, cause, the means of 'meeting Hari'. Bapura = poor, weak. Sahaai = help.

O Kabir! (It is true that the 'place' of peace for the mind is the holy company alone; to stay settled at Prabhu's feet, 'keep the company of the holy' — the holy company is the one and only means; but) if Parmatma Himself does not help (if Parmatma Himself does not come to dwell within the 'holy one', if the 'holy one' is not himself joined to Prabhu's feet), then this means, having become weak, is of no use.
Kabeer, what can the poor creature do, if the Lord does not give him assistance?
Kabir, what can the poor creature do, it the Lord assists him not?
Sri Kabir ji says: if Ram Himself does not help, what can this means, the poor being's effort of spiritual practice, do?
UN52: Jih jih = whichever. Dharau = I place. Pag = foot. Pag dharau = I place my foot, I take support. Mur mur jaai = keeps bending, keeps breaking, is itself being pressed down under some vice or other. ||97||

(To reach the top of the tree of lofty human life, the 'holy' are, as it were, branches; but the robed ones who only make disciples are weak branches.) Whichever (such) branch I place my foot on keeps breaking (being weak with selfishness). ||97||
Whatever branch he steps on breaks and collapses. ||97||
On whatever branch he places his foot, that one cracks, and breaks down.
Without Ram's help, whatever branch of spiritual practice one sets foot on, that very one bends and breaks; meaning, some obstacle comes in it. ||97||
0VY4: Avrah kau = to others. Mai = mah, in. Par hai = falls. Ret = (the word 'ret' is feminine, but even so the (u) stays at its end). (Note: talk of Parmatma's Name is, as it were, sugar; every being who hears it finds it sweet. But for those who only give teaching to others, these words are, as it were, mere sand; they themselves find no taste in them.)
O Kabir! The ('holy ones') who (only) give advice to others — sand falls into their mouth (no taste comes within them).
Kabeer, those who only preach to others - sand falls into their mouths.
Kabir falls into the mouth of those, who practise not what they preach to others.
Sri Kabir ji says: by teaching others without practising it oneself, only the sand of slander falls into one's mouth.
EX4R: Biraanee = another's, others'. Raas = capital. Raakhte = try to guard. Khet = crop, past earnings, all past virtues. ||98||

Such ('holy ones') try to guard the capital of others, but use up all their own past virtues (such 'holy ones' too are weak branches; they cannot raise anyone to the summit of humanity either). ||98||
They keep their eyes on the property of others, while their own farm is being eaten up. ||98||
They keep an eye on other's property, however, their own farm is being eaten up.

They guard the (raas) capital — the breaths — or the grain-heap of others, and the field of their own house has been eaten up. Meaning, they stop others from sins, and they themselves are engaged in sinful deeds with their body. ||98||
VY37: O Kabir! (Say: my longing is that) I may stay in the company of the Gurmukhs (even if my earnings shrink greatly), and get by eating the husks of barley.
Kabeer, I will remain in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, even if I have only coarse bread to eat.
Kabir, I will associate only with the saints, even if I may have to eat barley bread.
Sri Kabir ji says: even if one eats only the (bhoosee) husk of barley —
MZBL: Whatever hardship (of poverty and the like, from giving time to the holy company) comes, let it come. But may I not go into the company of people cut off from God. ||99||
Whatever will be, will be. I will not associate with the faithless cynics. ||99||
What is to be, let it happen. I shall associate not with the mammon worshippers.
for whatever is to happen will surely happen — never go into the company of the saakat. ||99||
DQ8A: Din din = day by day, as the days pass. Het = love (for Prabhu).
O Kabir! Staying in the company of the Gurmukhs, love for Parmatma grows and grows day by day.
Kabeer, in the Saadh Sangat, love for the Lord doubles day by day.
Kabir, associating with the saints, the Lord's love doubles day-by-day.
Sri Kabir ji says: through the company of the saints, love for Vahiguru doubles day by day.
W1B6: Kaaree = black. Kaanbree = blanket. Dhoe = by washing. Set = white. ||100||
But the person cut off from God is, as it were, a black blanket that never turns white even when washed. Staying in their company, purity of mind cannot be gained. ||100||
The faithless cynic is like a black blanket, which does not become white by being washed. ||100||
The infidel is like the black blanket that becomes not white by washing.

Saakat people are like a black blanket — meaning, of utterly impure inner mind — which never becomes white by washing; meaning, without chanting the Name, they are not purified by doing other deeds. ||100|| ☬ He speaks of those who shave their heads and call themselves paramhans:
K8JH: Moondia = shaved. Kaanh = for what? In vain.

O Kabir! (This person who goes about with shaven head thinking himself 'holy') has not shaved his mind (has not removed the dirt of vices from the mind); by shaving the hair of his head he has not become 'holy'.
Kabeer, you have not shaved your mind, so why do you shave your head?
Kabir, you have shaved not your mind, why shave you your hair.
Sri Kabir ji says: if one has not shaved the mind — meaning, has not made the mind free of desire — then what comes of shaving the hair?
69ZX: Whatever evil deed one is driven to, it is the mind that drives it; (if the head was shaved only to become 'holy', then) shaving the head is useless. ||101||
Whatever is done, is done by the mind; it is useless to shave your head. ||101||
Whatever is done that is done by the mind, so vain is your shaving the head.
For whatever has been done — meaning, every mischief done with desire — the mind has done; so the head that has been shaved is (ajaai) useless. ||101||
L6JK: Jaai = (if) it goes, (if) it perishes. Ta = then. Jaau = (in grammar a future imperative, singular, third person) let it go, let it perish, no matter if it perishes.
O Kabir! Never forget Parmatma's Name; (if, while remembering the Name, our) body and wealth begin to perish, let them perish.
Kabeer, do not abandon the Lord; your body and wealth shall go, so let them go.
Kabir, leave you not your Lord, however, if the body or wealth go, let those go.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, do not leave Ram's Name, and if body and wealth go, let them go.
2SZ7: Bedhia = pierced, (may it stay) pierced. Ramahi naam = in Ram's Name (Ramahi = Ramasya). Samaau = may it stay absorbed (future imperative, third person, singular). ||102||
But may our mind surely stay pierced by Prabhu's beautiful feet, surely stay absorbed in Parmatma's Name. ||102||
My consciousness is pierced by the Lord's Lotus Feet; I am absorbed in the Name of the Lord. ||102||
My mind is pierced through with the Lord's lotus feet and I am absorbed in His Name.
Those whose mind has (bedhia) met the lotus feet of Parmeshvar have merged into Ram, the Named One — that is, have become one with Him. ||102||
GH72: Jant = instrument, the musical instrument, attachment to the body, identification with the body. Toott gaee = have broken. Taar = the strings (of attachment), the strings of bodily attachment.

(If, even with 'body and wealth' gone, my mind stays absorbed 'in Ram's Name', this bargain is very cheap, because) O Kabir! The instrument of bodily attachment that I used to keep playing (having strayed from Parmatma's Name) — (now, through the blessing of remembering the Name,) all its strings (of attachment) have broken.
Kabeer, all the strings of the instrument I played are broken.
Kabir, all the strings of the instrument, which I played upon, are broken.

Sri Kabir ji says: the instrument of the threefold body that (ham) ego and the other beings used to play — that is, the perverse actions they used to cause — that instrument no longer plays. Why? Because all the strings of desire have broken from the inner mind.
3RGJ: Kia karai = can exert no force. Bajaavanhaar = the player, the one who plays the instrument (drum, music), who plays the drum of identification with the body; the mind that was playing the instrument of bodily attachment. ||103||

What can this poor instrument (of identification with the body) do (now)? That is, through the blessing of the Name, bodily attachment has been defeated. (Let alone bodily attachment,) the very mind that was playing the instrument of bodily attachment no longer remains. ||103||
What can the poor instrument do, when the player has departed as well. ||103||
What can the poor instrument do, when the player has departed?
What can the poor (jant) instrument do, when its players, ego and the rest, have gone? ||103||
6Z53: Maai moondau = I would shave the (head of the) mother. Tih = that. Ja te = from whom, by staying with whom, by walking on whose path. Bharam = the wandering of the mind, the wandering of bodily attachment, identification with the body. Na jaai = does not go away.

(This pandit holds me back from joining Parmatma's Name and, beating the drum of the ritual of his Vedas and other books of rites, wants to become my guru-priest; but) O Kabir! I would shave the head of such a guru's mother; by walking his path the wandering (of bodily attachment) cannot go away.
Kabeer, shave the mother of that guru, who does not take away one's doubt.
Kabir, shave you the mother of that Guru, through whom doubt departs not.
Sri Kabir ji says: shave the head of the mother of that false guru from whom the doubt of the mind does not go.

9VN3: These people themselves, caught in (the ritual of) the four Vedas, are drowned (in the deep waters of identification with the body); whoever follows them, they have swept them too into that same attachment. ||104||
He himself is drowning in the four Vedas; he drowns his disciples as well. ||104||
He himself is drowned in the four Vedas and drowns his disciples as well.
For they themselves are drowned in the ritual deeds told by the four Vedas, and they have swept their disciples too into the river of ritual. ||104||
MYC7: Jete = however many. Talai = below, within oneself. Duraai raakhe = kept hidden.

(Forgetting Parmatma's remembrance, a person falls into the current of bodily attachment and takes to the path of vices; with tilak, rosary, worship, loincloth and other religious garb, people may perhaps be convinced that these are devotees; but, straying from Prabhu's Name,) O Kabir! Whatever sins are committed (even if those sins) are kept hidden within oneself,
Kabeer, whatever sins the mortal has committed, he tries to keep hidden under cover.
Kabir, whatever sins the mortal commits, he tries to keep them hidden under s cover.
Sri Kabir ji says: all the sins this being had committed, it kept hidden under falsehood.
RHLR: still, when Dharamraj asks, those sins all come out in the end (that is, the ritual of the Vedas and the rest cannot save from vices; people may be convinced by outer religious garb, but inner sins cannot stay hidden from Parmatma). ||105||
But in the end, they shall all be revealed, when the Righteous Judge of Dharma investigates. ||105||
At last they are all disclosed, when the Lord-Justiciar holds and inquiry.
When Dharamrai questioned it, they all came out (nidaan) in the end. ||105||
3FN3: Rah gaia = the soul is left behind, the soul itself grows weak, the soul dies, the being dies a spiritual death. Na rahia = no one remained, no one is able to save, no one can rescue. Chhaad = leaving. Paalio bahut = kept providing for a long time, (did this all his life:) only kept providing (for the family).
O Kabir! It is the very result of giving up Parmatma's remembrance that a person spends all their life only providing for their family,
Kabeer, you have given up meditating on the Lord, and you have raised a large family.
Kabir, abandoning the Lord's meditation, you have reared a large family.
Sri Kabir ji says: this being, giving up Hari's remembrance, has provided for the family in many ways.
6332: doing the business of the world (for the family) (and, staying separated from Parmatma, the soul's companion,) in the end dies a spiritual death; no relative is able to save (from this spiritual death). ||106||
You continue to involve yourself in worldly affairs, but none of your brothers and relatives remain. ||106||
You continue to do worldly affairs, though none of yours brothers and kinsmen had remained stable.
The show for which one did business — wife, sons and the rest — stayed right here. Further on, in the next world, no helper remained; meaning, having eaten and drunk, they went their own way. ||106||
DUDB: Jagaavan jaai = goes to awaken (the cremation-ground spirits).
O Kabir! It is only because of staying without Parmatma's remembrance that (some childless, ignorant woman) goes at night (to the cremation ground) to awaken the spirits there.
Kabeer, those who give up meditation on the Lord, and get up at night to wake the spirits of the dead,
Kabir, abandoning the God's meditation, the woman, who wakes at night and goes to the cremation ground to practise witch craft;
Sri Kabir ji says: the woman who, giving up Hari's remembrance, out of longing for sons goes at night to awaken the cremation ground — meaning, does magic and spells —
6BDE: Autarai = descends, is born. Sarpan = she-snake. Hoe kai = becoming. Apune jaae = her own born children. Khaai = eats. ||107||
(But where is comfort from evil deeds? Such a woman, after losing her human birth,) is born a she-snake, and eats her own young. ||107||
shall be reincarnated as snakes, and eat their own offspring. ||107||
She is born as a serpent and eats her own offspring.
is born a she-snake and eats the sons she bore; meaning, by doing ill to others there is no comfort. ||107||
2B0A: Ahoee = the worship and fast of the goddess Sheetla in the month of Kattak. The gods and goddesses are held to have particular mounts: Ganesh's mount is the mouse, Brahma's the swan, Shiv's the white bull, Durga's the lion; in the same way Sheetla's mount is the donkey.
O Kabir! ('Do not leave Ram; if body and wealth go, let them go'; otherwise —) it is the very result of leaving Ram's Name that a (foolish) woman goes about keeping Sheetla's fast.
Kabeer, the woman who gives up meditation on the Lord, and observes the ritual fast of Ahoi,
Kabir, abandoning the Lord's meditation, if a woman observes the fast of the smallpox-Goddess,
Sri Kabir ji says: the woman who, giving up Hari's remembrance, worships (ahoee) Sheetla and keeps her fast —
C231: Gadhee = she-donkey. Man chaar = four maunds. ||108||

(And if Sheetla should love her very much, she will make her into her own mount, the she-donkey, to keep her with her always.) So that foolish woman enters the birth of a she-donkey and carries a load of four maunds (like other donkeys, of sacks and the like). ||108||
shall be reincarnated as a donkey, to carry heavy burdens. ||108||
she is then reborn as a she-donkey and carries a load of four maunds.
is born a she-donkey and bears a load of four maunds on her back. As it says: ☬ "One who runs after Bhairau, ghosts and Sheetla, ☬ riding a donkey, kicks up the dust." ||108||
YF99: O Kabir! (To escape the fears, doubts and superstitions of the world,) the greatest wisdom of all is to remember Parmatma's Name within the heart itself.
Kabeer, it is the most clever wisdom, to chant and meditate on the Lord in the heart.
Kabir, exceedingly great wisdom is in this, that man should remember God in his mind.
Sri Kabir ji says: to chant Hari's Name with the tongue and meditate on it in the heart — that alone is great cleverness.
UR8M: (But) this remembrance is no easy task; (pride of caste, slander, bad company, cravings, fasts and other superstitions have to be given up; so) remembering Prabhu is like mounting the gallows; and falling from this gallows (that is, giving up this very hard task of remembrance) does no good either, because without remembrance there is no other support (to escape the pains, troubles and fears of the world). ||109||
It is like playing on a pig; if you fall off, you will find no place of rest. ||109||
The Lord's meditation is like playing on the noose and if man falls from it, then finds he no place of rest.
But this chanting of Hari is as hard as moving about on top of a stake. For the one who falls from that Name there is no place to stand; meaning, there are many obstacles in devotion. ||109||
TGSD: Soee = (the letter 's' carries two vowel signs, (o) and (u); the original word is 'soee'; here, to keep the metre of the salok, it is read 'suee'. (o) has two measures; here one measure is dropped and it is read as (u).) Dhann = fortunate.
(So) O Kabir! That mouth alone is fortunate with which Ram's Name is uttered.
Kabeer, blessed is that mouth, which utters the Lord's Name.
Kabir, blessed is the mouth, with which mouth the Lord's Name is recited.
Sri Kabir ji says: the mouth from which Ram's Name is spoken — that mouth alone is worthy to be called blessed.
90ET: Dehee = body. Baapuree = poor. Graam = village. ||110||
What to speak of that poor body? (The body becoming pure is a small thing; let alone that body,) the whole village where the person lives who remembers the Name becomes pure. ||110||
It purifies the body, and the whole village as well. ||110||
What to say of the poor body of that creature, even his village shall be purified.
What is it for the poor body to become pure by uttering that Ram's Name? Where the Name is uttered, the very village becomes pure. ||110||
7JYU: O Kabir! The lineage in which a devotee who remembers Parmatma appears — that lineage alone is blessed.
Kabeer, that family is good, in which the Lord's slave is born.
Kabir, blessed is the family, is which family God's slave is born.
Sri Kabir ji says: that lineage alone is good in which a servant of Hari is born.
B29G: Oopjai = (Sanskrit jan, with upa; upajan = to become visible, to appear, to grow) to appear. ||111||
The lineage in which no person who worships Prabhu appears — (know) that lineage (to be as fruitless as useless trees like) dhak and palaah. ||111||
But that family in which the Lord's slave is not born is as useless as weeds. ||111||
The family, is which the Lord's slave is born not; that family is useless like the buteafrondosa.
The lineage in which no servant of Hari is born is like a (dhaak) crowd of (palaas) chhichhra trees; meaning, it is useless. ||111||
VCKW: Hai = haya, horses. Gai = gai, gaya, gaja, elephants. Baahan = mounts (for riding). Saghan ghan = countless. Dhaja = flags. Phahraahi = flutter, wave in the wind.

O Kabir! If there are countless horses and elephants to ride, if hundreds of thousands of flags flutter (over the palaces) (even with such splendour, without Parmatma's Name this kingdom and fortune are of no use).
Kabeer, some have lots of horses, elephants and carriages, and thousands of banners waving.
Kabir, the possession of very great number of horses, elephants and carriages and the waving of lacs of banners;

Sri Kabir ji says: even if one has very dense (ghan) cavalcades of (hai) horses and (gai) elephants, and so much wealth — a flag is raised for every ten million — that hundreds of thousands of such flags flutter, and in such comfort one is without Hari's Name —
2QUH: Bhikhya = the food holy men and faqirs beg from the door of householders. (Under the letter 'kh' is a half 'y'.) Jau = if. Jaahi = pass. Te = than. ||112||
If the days (of life) pass in remembering Parmatma, then better than the comfort (of kingdom without remembrance) is the crust that begging faqirs eat, asked from people's doors. ||112||
But begging is better than these comforts, if one spends his days meditating in remembrance on the Lord. ||112||
Begging is better than these comforts, if the days pass in contemplating the Lord.
then better than the comfort of these things is begging alms and eating, if by eating them the days pass in remembering Hari. ||112||
1856: Maandal = drum. Kandh = on the shoulders. Chadhaai = placing.

O Kabir! With a drum on my shoulders I (went about beating it and) have searched the whole world (I went about asking, "Tell me, brother, has anyone seen any companion who lasts to the end among this kingdom and fortune, mansions and palaces, kin and relatives?" But no one said yes).
Kabeer, I have wandered all over the world, carrying the drum on my shoulder.
Kabir, carrying the drum on my shoulder, I have traversed the whole world.
Sri Kabir ji says: lifting the (maandal) drum of the Shastras onto my (kandh) shoulders — that is, holding them in the heart — I have wandered through the whole world.
TWQ0: Kaahoo ko = anyone's. Sabh = all (creation). Thok bajaai = testing thoroughly. ||113||
(So) I have tested all creation thoroughly: no one is anyone's (companion to the end) (the true companion is Parmatma's Name alone; so 'do not leave Ram; if body and wealth go, let them go'). ||113||
No one belongs to anyone else; I have looked and carefully studied it. ||113||
No one is the friend of any one else, I have seen and carefully examined all.
No one is anyone's helper. I have looked over all creation, knocking and tapping — that is, examining it. ||113||
UUE3: Maarag = on the road. Beethre = are scattered. Niksio aai = has come by chance.

(Parmatma's virtues are, as it were,) pearls (scattered) on the road (of the journey of human life) (that is, no wealth has to be spent to take these pearls; but here an) ignorant, blind person has come.
The pearls are scattered on the road; the blind man comes along.
Kabir, the pearls are scattered on the road and a blind man comes that way.

O brother! On the road to Hari, which is the Shastras, the pearls of good virtues are spread about. The being blinded by ignorance has come and passed along there too; meaning, even though they read the Shastras —
5908: Jot = light. Jagdees = jagat-ees, Prabhu, Master of the world. Ulanghe jaai = keeps stepping over, keeps trampling (those pearls) underfoot. ||114||

Without the light (of knowledge) given by Parmatma, the world goes on trampling these pearls underfoot (a person does not value singing Parmatma's praise; only if Prabhu Himself shows mercy can this being sing His virtues). ||114||
Without the Light of the Lord of the Universe, the world just passes them by. ||114||
Without the Light of the Lord of the universe, the mortal passes the pearls by.

yet without the (jot) knowledge of Jagdishvar, they pass over those pearls of good virtues in the world; meaning, giving up virtues, they take to faults. ||114|| ☬ A rich man's son died. Kabir ji's son Kamaal brought him back to life. Then that rich man brought a great deal of wealth and set it before him. Kamaal took that wealth to his own house. Seeing that deed, Sri Kabir ji said for Kamaal's sake:
0SP3: Booda = drowned (know it). Bans = lineage, family (all the senses, eyes, ears, nose and the rest), household. Upjio = (see salok 111) appeared, reached this state. Poot = son, mind. Kamaal = accomplished, worthy, wondrously worthy (that is, unworthy, foolish).

(I have seen that among 'countless horses and elephants to ride' and 'hundreds of thousands of flags' 'no one is anyone's' — 'I have tested it thoroughly'; even so,) if my foolish mind has come down to (a low) state, then know that the whole household of me, Kabir (the whole crew of senses, eyes, ears, nose and the rest) has (surely) drowned (in vices),
My family is drowned, O Kabeer, since the birth of my son Kamaal.
Kabir, drowned is my family, when my son Kamal was born.
"Our lineage has drowned, because, O Kamaal, you have been born a son in our house.
KS7H: Ghar = in the house, in the heart, within oneself. Maal = wealth, longing for wealth, attachment to Maya (to understand this sense, read saloks 112 and 113). ||115||
because, giving up Parmatma's remembrance, I have settled attachment to Maya within myself. ||115||
He has given up meditating on the Lord, in order to bring home wealth. ||115||
Forsaking the God's meditation, he has brought home wealth.

Giving up Hari's remembrance, you have brought wealth and goods into the house" — meaning, you have broken Hari's command. Hearing this, Kamaal fell at his feet and had his fault forgiven. Or: the lineage of good virtues of the (kabir) great being has drowned, since the son that is the (kamaal) mind has been born. What is that mind like? Giving up Hari's remembrance, it has brought wealth and goods into the heart; meaning, it is holding the things of the world in the heart. ||115||
9FUY: Saadhoo = a good person, one who has tamed their own mind, a Gurmukh.

O Kabir! ('Do not leave Ram; if body and wealth go, let them go'; but Prabhu's Name is found only from those who have kept their mind tamed, who are themselves 'holy'; so one should keep the company of the 'holy'; but) if we go to see some holy Gurmukh, we should not take anyone along (we should not wait for company or look for supports for going, lest some companion bound by attachment cause delay).
Kabeer, go out to meet the holy man; do not take anyone else with you.
Kabir, when you go to meet the saint, take not another with you,
Sri Kabir ji says: when we go to meet the saints, let us not take any desire along — that is, let us go free of desire.
TURA: Aagai = while going towards the holy one, while staying face to face with some Gurmukh. Hoe su hoe = if any hardship comes, let it come. ||116||
Going to see some Gurmukh, let us never step back (never be lazy); rather, if some hardship comes while going there, let it come. ||116||
Do not turn back - keep on going. Whatever will be, will be. ||116||
then turn you not your foot backward and march on ahead., and whatever else happens, let that happen.

Again, let us not set the (paau) foot of the intellect back towards the world. Going forward towards Parmeshvar, whatever happens, let it happen; meaning, stay even in what is wanted and unwanted. ||116||
3M0B: Jih jevree = with which rope, with which rope of possessiveness, with the rope of attachment to Maya. Tih = with that rope. Mat bandhahu = do not get bound.
O Kabir! Do not let yourself be bound by the rope of attachment to Maya with which the world (every being in it) is bound.
Kabeer, do not bind yourself with that chain, which binds the whole world.
Kabir, blind you not yourself with the chain, with which the world is bound.
Sri Kabir ji says: O brother, do not get bound by the (kabir) great rope of desire with which the whole world is bound.
KEHZ: Jai hahi = you will be ruined. Aata lon jiu = like flour and salt, at a cheap price. Son samaan = like gold, precious. Sareer = human body. ||117||

This (precious) human body (that you have been given) is like gold; (if, bound by the rope of attachment and staying away from the company of the Gurmukhs, you give up Parmatma's remembrance, then) you will be ruined for nothing, cheaply. ||117||
As the salt is lost in the flour, so shall your golden body be lost. ||117||
As the salt is lost in flour, so shall your gold like body disappear.
For this human body will dissolve like a (aata) lump of salt — that is, perish. (So) it takes no longer than that lump of salt; meaning, the body perishes very fast. ||117||
4SDX: Hans = the soul. Udio = wants to fly, is preparing to leave the body. Tan gaadio = the body is about to be buried; the separation of body and soul is at hand. Sojhaaee = understanding. Sainaah = with signs.

(This rope of possessiveness is no ordinary bond.) O Kabir! (If you want to understand the state of those who, straying from Parmatma's remembrance, are bound by the rope of attachment to Maya, then see: death arrives overhead;) the soul is about to leave (the body), the body is about to collapse (on the soul's departure); even so, the being bound by the rope of attachment still explains (to the relatives left behind) by signs,
Kabeer, the soul-swan is flying away, and the body is being buried, and still he makes gestures.
Kabir, when the soul-swan is about to fly and the body is about to be bruised, even then mortal instructs with gestures.

Sri Kabir ji says: the swan of the soul has got ready to fly, and its body is about to be buried — meaning, death has come near — and still it does not (sojha) come to understand (eesai) Vahiguru; or, even then it explains to relatives by (sainaah) signs where its buried things are.
TRU3: Rankaaee = meanness, poverty. Nainaah = of the eyes. ||118||
(even at that time Prabhu does not come to mind); even now the being does not give up the poverty of the eyes. ||118||
Even then, the mortal does not give up the cruel look in his eyes. ||118||
Even then, the mortal leaves not the meanness of his eyes.
Even in this state this being does not give up the poverty of the eyes. ||118||
9MV0: Nain nihaarau = may I see with the eyes. Tujh kau = You (O Prabhu!). Sravan = with the ears. Sunau = may I hear.

O Kabir! (Pray at Prabhu's door and say: "O Prabhu! Forgetting You, the world is bound by the rope of attachment and does not give up the poverty of the eyes even at the time of death; show mercy, that, to escape that rope,) I may keep seeing You alone with my eyes (everywhere), may keep hearing Your Name alone with my ears,
Kabeer: with my eyes, I see You, Lord; with my ears, I hear Your Name.
Kabir, O my Lord, with my eyes I see You and with my ears hear I Your Name.
Sri Kabir ji says: O Vahiguru! May I always see You alone with my eyes, and always hear Your Name alone with my ears.
SAXL: Tua = Your. Bain = words, through words. Ucharau = may I utter. Jee = O Prabhu ji! Charan kamal = Your feet, beautiful as lotus flowers. Thaau = place. ||119||
may keep uttering Your Name alone in words (with the tongue), and may keep giving Your beautiful feet a place in my heart." ||119||
With my tongue I chant Your Name; I enshrine Your Lotus Feet within my heart. ||119||
With my tongue I recite Your Name and enshrine Yours lotus feet within my mind.
With all my heart may I keep uttering Your Name with the tongue, and may Your lotus feet dwell in the place of the heart too. ||119||
N6CT: Te = from. Rahio = have been saved. Parsaad = by the grace.
O Kabir! By my True Guru's grace I have been saved from (longing for) heaven and (fear of) hell.
Kabeer, I have been spared from heaven and hell, by the Grace of the True Guru.
Kabir, by the True Guru's grace, I have escaped from paradise and hell.
Sri Kabir ji says: by the True Guru being pleased, I have become free of heaven and hell.
34ZW: Mauj = wave, surge of joy. Ant ar aad = from beginning to end, always. ||120||
I stay always in the surge of joy of (the remembrance of) Parmatma's beautiful feet. ||120||
From beginning to end, I abide in the joy of the Lord's Lotus Feet. ||120||
In enjoy abiding in the Lord's lotus feet, in the beginning and at the end.
So I stay in the joy of that True Guru's lotus feet, beginning and end — that is, always. ||120||
W93B: Mauj ko = of the wave, of the surge of joy. Kah = may tell, may say. Kaise = how? Unmaan = (Sanskrit unmaan = measuring, price) weight, estimate, worth.
(But) O Kabir! How can anyone tell the measure of the joy of staying settled at Prabhu's beautiful feet?
Kabeer, how can I even describe the extent of the joy of the Lord's Lotus Feet?
Kabir, how can I tell you, the extent of the joy of the Lord's lotus feet?
Sri Kabir ji says: how can I tell the joy of those lotus feet by estimate? Meaning, to what can I compare it? That is, nothing is like it.
WY4S: Kahibe kau = by describing. Parvaan = authentic, worth accepting. ||121||
Describing that joy (with the tongue) does not do it justice; how great a joy is it? One is satisfied only by experiencing that joy. ||121||
I cannot describe its sublime glory; it has to be seen to be appreciated. ||121||
Its sublimity can be described not. it can only be seen and realised.
Speaking of it does not do it justice; only seeing is acceptable. Meaning, it is not in mere words; whoever sees it, that alone is accepted. ||121||
RNVL: Kih = what? Kahau = may I say. Pateeaai = is convinced, is satisfied, finds joy.
O Kabir! Having seen that Prabhu, I cannot tell anything, and by telling no one can be satisfied either (because there is nothing in the world to which one could point and say Parmatma is like this),
Kabeer, how can I describe what I have seen? No one will believe my words.
Kabir, seeing my Lord, how can I describe Him? No one can be satisfied with my words.
Sri Kabir ji says: having seen Him, to whom shall I tell it, since no one believes what is told?
C81J: Rahau = I stay. Harakh = in joy, in bliss. Gaai = singing. ||122||
Parmatma is like Himself alone; (I can only say that) singing and singing His virtues I stay settled in joy. ||122||
The Lord is just as He is. I dwell in delight, singing His Glorious Praises. ||122||
As God is, so is He Himself alone. I abide in the delight of singing His praises.
So as Hari is, so He alone is; meaning, there is no other equal to Hari. Singing His virtues I stay always full of (harakh) bliss. ||122||
